title.zh: 卷263 列傳五十 王宏祚 姚文然 魏象枢 朱之弼 赵申乔
title.en: Volume 263 Biographies 50: Wang Hongzuo, Yao Wenran, Wei Xiangshu, Zhu Zhibi, Zhao Shenqiao
title.raw: 卷263 列傳五十 王宏祚 姚文然 魏象枢 朱之弼 赵申乔

sentences.zh: 王弘祚，字懋自，雲南永昌人。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzuo, style name Maozi, was a man of Yongchang in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzuo, whose style was Maozi, came from Yongchang in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎三年舉人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen of the Ming he was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 自薊州知州遷戶部郎中，督餉大同。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Jizhou he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and supervised grain supplies at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as magistrate of Jizhou, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and put in charge of provisioning the army at Datong.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授岢嵐兵備道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed military preparedness commissioner of Kelan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he was made military preparedness commissioner at Kelan.

sentences.zh: 總督吳孳昌以弘祚籌畫軍餉，請仍留大同。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Zichang, because Hongzuo had planned military provisions, requested that he still remain at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Zichang asked that Hongzuo stay on at Datong, since he had been so effective at organizing military supplies.

sentences.zh: 二年，以總督李鑑薦，仍授戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the recommendation of Governor-General Li Jian, he was again appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on Li Jian's recommendation as governor-general, he was reappointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 中原初定，圖籍散佚。

translations.literal: When the Central Plains had just been pacified, registers and archives were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains had only just been pacified, and land registers and archives lay scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 弘祚聰強習掌故，戶部疏請修賦役全書，以弘祚主其事。

translations.literal: Hongzuo was intelligent and strong and versed in precedents; the Ministry of Revenue memorialized to compile the Complete Book of Land Tax and Corvée, with Hongzuo directing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo was exceptionally able and steeped in administrative precedent, so the Ministry of Revenue memorialized to compile the Complete Book of Land Tax and Corvée and put him in charge.

sentences.zh: 弘祚謂：「民不苦正供而苦雜派，法不立則吏不畏，吏不畏則民不安。

translations.literal: Hongzuo said: "The people do not suffer from regular levies but from miscellaneous exactions; if law is not established then clerks do not fear, if clerks do not fear then the people are not secure.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo argued: "The people are not crushed by regular taxes but by assorted surcharges; without fixed law the clerks feel no restraint, and when clerks feel no restraint the people cannot live in peace.

sentences.zh: 閭閻菽帛之輸，朝廷悉知之，則可以艱難成節儉。

translations.literal: If the court fully knows the grain and cloth submitted from every household, then thrift can be achieved amid hardship.
translations.idiomatic: If the court knows exactly what every household pays in grain and cloth, thrift can be practiced even in hard times.

sentences.zh: 版籍賦稅之事，小民悉知之，則可以燭照絕侵漁。」

translations.literal: If the common people fully know matters of registers and taxation, then encroachment and extortion can be entirely cut off by illumination."
translations.idiomatic: If ordinary people understand register and tax matters as well, official encroachment and extortion can be stopped cold by full transparency."

sentences.zh: 裁定賦役，一準萬曆間法例，晚末苛細巧取，盡芟除之，以為一代程式。

translations.literal: He fixed land tax and corvée, uniformly following the legal examples of the Wanli period; the harsh and finicky levies of the late [dynasty] were all cut away, and this became the model code for a generation.
translations.idiomatic: He then fixed land tax and corvée on the Wanli statutes alone, cutting away every harsh and finicky levy of the dynasty's last years, and made this the standard code for the new reign.

sentences.zh: 三年，加太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional post of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he received the additional post of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷太僕寺卿，仍領郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud, still retaining his post as Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud while still holding his post as Director.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時雲、貴尚為明守，孫可望據辰州。

translations.literal: At the time Yunnan and Guizhou were still held by Ming loyalists, and Sun Kewang held Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan and Guizhou were still in Ming loyalist hands, and Sun Kewang held Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘祚請於江南、江西、湖廣豐稔之地，採米穀、儲糧餉為進取計。

translations.literal: Hongzuo requested that in the fertile regions of Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Huguang grain be collected and provisions stored for a plan of advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo proposed gathering grain in the fertile districts of Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Huguang and stockpiling provisions for the coming offensive.

sentences.zh: 又言：「黔國公沐天波世守雲南，得民心，其僚屬有散處江寧者，宜令往招天波為內應。

translations.literal: He also said: "Duke Mu Tianbo of Guizhou had long guarded Yunnan and won the people's hearts; there are subordinates of his scattered in Jiangning—it is fitting to order them to go and summon Tianbo as an insider response.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that Duke Mu Tianbo of Guizhou, whose family had long held Yunnan and enjoyed popular support, still had followers scattered in Jiangning who should be sent to win Tianbo over as an inside ally.

sentences.zh: 貴州九股黑苗，自都勻、黎平遠及慶遠、靖州，近為可望蹂躪，宜加意撫綏，俾令歸化。

translations.literal: The Nine-Stock Black Miao of Guizhou, from Duyun and Liping far to Qingyuan and Jingzhou, have lately been trampled by Kewang; deliberate soothing and pacification should be applied to bring them to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine-Stock Black Miao of Guizhou, ranging from Duyun and Liping to distant Qingyuan and Jingzhou, had lately been ravaged by Kewang; they deserved careful pacification to bring them back under the throne.

sentences.zh: 冠服異制，勿驟更易。」

translations.literal: Their caps and clothing differ in form—do not change them all at once."
translations.idiomatic: Their dress and customs differed from ours and should not be changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 上以所言足助撫剿，下經略大學士洪承疇採行。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered his words sufficient to aid pacification and suppression and transmitted them to Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, coordinator of the campaign, for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found these proposals sound aids to pacification and suppression and forwarded them to Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, the campaign coordinator, for action.

sentences.zh: 十一年，給事中郭一鶚劾弘祚修賦役全書逾久未成，弘祚疏辨，一鶚复劾其巧飾。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Censor Guo Yihu memorialized that Hongzuo had taken too long without completing the Complete Book; Hongzuo memorialized in rebuttal, and Guo again memorialized that he was artfully glossing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Supervising Secretary Guo Yihu accused Hongzuo of dragging out the Complete Book without finishing it; Hongzuo rebutted in a memorial, and Guo accused him again of clever evasions.

sentences.zh: 下部議，以各省冊報稽遲，弘祚不舉劾，論罰俸。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation; because each province's returns were tardy and Hongzuo had not impeached [officials], he was sentenced to forfeiture of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the ministries for review; because provincial registers arrived late and Hongzuo had failed to impeach the delinquents, he was fined a year's salary.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏請禁有司私派累民、將領冒名領餉，皆下部議行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized to forbid local officials' private exactions burdening the people and generals' claiming rations under false names; all were referred to the ministries and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized to ban private surcharges by local officials and false-name ration claims by generals; both measures were referred to the ministries and enacted.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以河西務鈔關員外郎硃世德徵稅不如額，援赦請免議，坐降三級，命留任。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, because Zhu Shide, an outside-section vice director at the Hexiwu paper-tax customs on the canal, collected taxes below quota and invoked amnesty to escape censure, [Hongzuo] was demoted three ranks but ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Zhu Shide, an outside-section vice director at the Hexiwu canal customs, fell short of his tax quota yet invoked an amnesty to escape censure, Hongzuo was demoted three ranks but allowed to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 十五年，賦役全書成，敘勞，還所降級。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the Complete Book of Land Tax and Corvée was finished; for merit in labor his demotion was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the Complete Book was finished; his service was rewarded and his demotion reversed.

sentences.zh: 考滿，廕子。

translations.literal: When his term assessment was complete, a son was ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: When his term assessment ended, a son received hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 尋擢尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Minister and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a ministry director and given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 命同大學士巴哈納等校訂律例。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others to collate and revise the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Grand Secretary Bahana and others in revising the penal code.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進太子太保。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was advanced to Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 雲南平，迭疏上善後諸事，請開鄉試，慎署員，設重鎮，稽丁田，卹士紳，撫土司，寬新政。

translations.literal: When Yunnan was pacified, he repeatedly memorialized on various post-pacification matters, requesting restoration of the provincial examination, careful appointment of officials, establishment of heavy garrisons, verification of households and fields, relief for gentry, pacification of native chiefs, and leniency in new policies.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunnan was pacified he sent a stream of memorials on reconstruction: restore the provincial examinations, appoint officials carefully, post strong garrisons, verify households and fields, relieve the gentry, pacify native chiefs, and temper new policies.

sentences.zh: 既，又疏言司道宜久任，州縣宜部選，投誠宜解散，荒殘宜軫卹，爐座宜多設。

translations.literal: Later he again memorialized that circuit intendants should serve long terms, prefects and magistrates should be appointed by the ministry, surrendered forces should be disbanded, desolate ruins should receive relief, and furnace posts should be increased.
translations.idiomatic: He later added that circuit officials should serve longer terms, prefects and magistrates should be centrally appointed, surrendered troops disbanded, devastated regions relieved, and smelting posts expanded.

sentences.zh: 弘祚聞父母喪，疏乞解官奔赴，命在任守制。

translations.literal: Hongzuo heard that his parents had died and memorialized begging leave from office to go mourn; he was ordered to observe mourning while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: When both parents died Hongzuo asked to leave office and go home to mourn; he was ordered to observe mourning without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 踰月，命出視事。

translations.literal: After a month he was ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was told to return to duty.

sentences.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，疏請歸葬，許之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Sacred Ancestor took the throne, he memorialized requesting permission to return home for burial; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, after the Kangxi emperor's accession, he asked leave to go home and bury his parents; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 旋諭促還朝。

translations.literal: Soon he was instructed to hasten back to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to hurry back to court.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，授刑部尚書，尋復還戶部。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he was appointed Minister of Justice, then soon restored to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi he was made Minister of Justice, then soon returned to head the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四年，星變地震，求直言。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on a strange star and earthquake, [the court] sought forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after omens in the heavens and an earthquake, the court called for candid memorials.

sentences.zh: 弘祚疏言：「異星見，天失其常；

translations.literal: Hongzuo memorialized: "When a strange star appears, Heaven has lost its constancy;
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo wrote: "When a strange star appears, Heaven has lost its proper order;

sentences.zh: 地震，地失其常。

translations.literal: when the earth quakes, Earth has lost its constancy.
translations.idiomatic: when the earth quakes, Earth has lost its proper order.

sentences.zh: 挽回天地之變，首在率循人事之常。」

translations.literal: To turn back Heaven and Earth's changes, the first step lies in leading and following the constancy of human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: To turn back such changes in Heaven and Earth, we must first restore constancy in human affairs."

sentences.zh: 漕糧自通州運京師，或謂水次支散，可省轉搬費。

translations.literal: Tribute grain was transported from Tongzhou to the capital; some said disbursement at the waterfront could save transfer costs.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute grain was shipped from Tongzhou to the capital; some argued that paying it out at the landing could save transshipment costs.

sentences.zh: 弘祚持不可，謂：「水次支散，受者艱負戴。

translations.literal: Hongzuo held this impermissible, saying: "If disbursed at the waterfront, recipients would struggle to carry it on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo objected, arguing: "If grain were paid out at the wharf, recipients would struggle to carry it away.

sentences.zh: 必減直而售，則米狼戾在外。

translations.literal: They would have to reduce the price to sell, and then grain would be scattered outside in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They would have to cut prices to sell it, and grain would flood the markets outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 京倉頒給雖有糶​​者，顆粒皆在都下。

translations.literal: Although the capital granaries distributed and there were sellers, every grain stayed within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Even when capital granaries sold grain, every kernel remained within the city.

sentences.zh: 根本至計，不宜以小利遽變。」

translations.literal: This is a policy of fundamental security; it should not be hastily changed for a small gain."
translations.idiomatic: This is a matter of fundamental security and must not be overturned for a minor saving."

sentences.zh: 又有議盡裁州縣存留與變漕糧官運為商運者，固爭不得，具疏上之，卒如弘祚議。

translations.literal: There were also proposals to cut entirely prefectural and county retained funds and to change official transport of tribute grain to merchant transport; he firmly opposed and could not prevail, but after memorializing in full the Emperor finally followed Hongzuo's view.
translations.idiomatic: Others proposed abolishing prefectural and county retained funds and switching tribute transport from official to merchant carriage; he fought both proposals, memorialized at length, and the emperor ultimately sided with him.

sentences.zh: 六年，用輔政大臣鼇拜議，戶部增設滿尚書，以授瑪爾賽，與弘祚齟《齒吾》。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on the recommendation of Oboi, a ranking grand secretary, the Ministry of Revenue added a Manchu minister and Ma'er Sai was appointed; he and Hongzuo clashed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, on regent Oboi's advice, a Manchu minister was added to the Ministry of Revenue and Ma'er Sai was appointed; he and Hongzuo were constantly at odds.

sentences.zh: 七年，戶部失察書吏假印盜帑，大學士班布爾善獨罪弘祚，坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Ministry failed to detect clerks' forging seals to steal treasury funds; Grand Secretary Banbursan alone blamed Hongzuo, who was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the ministry failed to catch clerks who forged seals and stole from the treasury; Grand Secretary Banbursan laid all blame on Hongzuo, who was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 八年，鼇拜得罪，起弘祚兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Oboi fell from power and Hongzuo was raised to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after Oboi's fall, Hongzuo was recalled as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 九年，以老乞休，命馳驛歸里，食原俸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on grounds of age he begged retirement; he was ordered to return home by courier post and draw his original salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he retired on grounds of age and was sent home by imperial courier, keeping his full salary.

sentences.zh: 弘祚中道疾作，僑居江寧。

translations.literal: Hongzuo fell ill on the road and took lodging in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo fell ill on the journey and settled temporarily in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 念未終事父母，輯永思錄，自號曰思齋。

translations.literal: Mindful that he had not finished serving his parents, he compiled the Eternal Recollection Record and styled himself Sizhai (Reflection Studio).
translations.idiomatic: Brooding that he had never fully served his parents, he compiled the Eternal Recollection Record and took the sobriquet Sizhai, Studio of Remembrance.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏辭俸，諭曰：「卿在官著有勞績，引年乞休，賜祿頤養，毋固辭。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized declining salary; the edict said: "You achieved merit in office; citing age to retire, salary is granted to support your old age—do not firmly decline."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he declined his stipend; the emperor replied: "Your service has been distinguished; now that you retire on account of age, keep your salary for your comfort—do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒，賜祭葬，諡端簡。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died; funeral sacrifice and burial were granted, posthumous title Duānjian (Upright and Concise).
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died; state funeral honors were granted and he was posthumously titled Duānjian, Upright and Concise.

sentences.zh: 姚文然，字弱侯，江南桐城人。

translations.literal: Yao Wenran, style name Ruohou, was a native of Tongcheng in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wenran, whose style was Ruohou, came from Tongcheng in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎十六年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen of the Ming he passed the metropolitan examination and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen and entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，以安慶巡撫李猶龍薦，授國史院庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Anqing grand coordinator Li Youlong, he was appointed Hanlin bachelor of the Historiography Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, on Li Youlong's recommendation as grand coordinator of Anqing, he was appointed a Hanlin bachelor in the Historiography Academy.

sentences.zh: 五年，改禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏請「敕撫、按、道恩詔清理刑獄，勿任有司稽玩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized requesting: "Order grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and circuit intendants in the amnesty edict to clear prisons and not let local officials delay and trifle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he asked that grand coordinators, surveillance commissioners, and circuit intendants be ordered, under the amnesty edict, to clear the prisons and stop local officials from stalling.

sentences.zh: 條赦之外，有可矜疑原宥者，許專疏上陳」。

translations.literal: Beyond the amnesty articles, where there are cases meriting pity, doubt, or pardon, allow special memorials to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the amnesty list, cases that merit pity, doubt, or pardon should be allowed separate memorials to the throne."

sentences.zh: 又請重定會試下第舉人選用例，以廣任使。

translations.literal: He also requested reestablishing regulations for use of candidates who failed the metropolitan examination, to broaden appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that rules for appointing candidates who failed the metropolitan examination be redrawn to widen the pool of usable talent.

sentences.zh: 又言：「直隸與山東、河南接壤，盜賊竊發，東西竄匿，難於越境追捕。

translations.literal: He also said: "Zhili borders Shandong and Henan; bandits steal out sporadically and flee east and west, making cross-border pursuit difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Zhili bordered Shandong and Henan, so bandits could strike and flee across provincial lines, making pursuit difficult.

sentences.zh: 請改保定巡撫為總督，轄直隸、山東及河南懷慶、衛輝、彰德三府。」

translations.literal: Request to change the Baoding grand coordinator into a governor-general with jurisdiction over Zhili, Shandong, and the three prefectures Huaiqing, Weihui, and Zhangde in Henan."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed elevating the Baoding grand coordinator to governor-general over Zhili, Shandong, and Henan's Huaiqing, Weihui, and Zhangde prefectures."

sentences.zh: 又請敕各省督撫勿濫委私人署州縣官。

translations.literal: He also requested ordering each province's governor-generals and grand coordinators not to indiscriminately deputize private persons to act as prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that provincial governors and grand coordinators be forbidden to let private associates act as prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 諸疏皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All memorials were referred to the ministries and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All these memorials were referred to the ministries and carried out.

sentences.zh: 尋轉工科。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Works [as supervising secretary].
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖親政，疏請令都察院甄別各省巡按，下部院會議，以六等考核，黜陟有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Shizu Emperor personally took power, he memorialized requesting the Censorate to evaluate provincial surveillance commissioners; the ministries and boards met and used six grades for assessment, with dismissals and promotions varying.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Shunzhi emperor took personal rule, he asked the Censorate to grade provincial surveillance commissioners; the ministries met, ranked them in six classes, and promoted or dismissed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 是歲，江南、浙江被水，文然請災地漕米改折，視災重輕定折多寡。

translations.literal: That year Jiangnan and Zhejiang suffered flooding; Wenran requested that in disaster areas tribute grain be converted to cash payment, with the conversion rate fixed according to severity of disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That year floods struck Jiangnan and Zhejiang; Wenran asked that tribute grain in stricken districts be commuted to cash, with rates set by the severity of the disaster.

sentences.zh: 既，又言：「折漕例新定，民未周知。

translations.literal: Later he again said: "The tribute conversion rule was newly fixed and the people do not fully know it.
translations.idiomatic: He later warned that the new grain-commutation rules were not yet widely understood.

sentences.zh: 官吏或折外重徵耗銀，或先已徵米而又收折，或折重運輕，其弊不一。

translations.literal: Officials may levy extra shortage silver beyond the conversion, or have already collected grain and again collect conversion, or convert heavy and transport light—the abuses are not one kind.
translations.idiomatic: Officials might levy extra fees beyond the commutation, collect grain and then collect commutation cash as well, or set high commutation rates while delivering light grain—the abuses took many forms.

sentences.zh: 請敕漕臣密察嚴劾。」

translations.literal: Request that tribute officials secretly investigate and strictly impeach."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that grain transport officials investigate in secret and impeach offenders strictly."

sentences.zh: 上並採納。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 十年，疏言大臣得罪不當鎖禁，得旨允行。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he memorialized that great ministers who offended should not be shackled; the directive was approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he argued that disgraced high ministers should not be put in chains; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 遷兵科都給事中，乞歸養。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of War and begged leave to nurse [parents].
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief supervising secretary in the Ministry of War and asked to go home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，起補戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi he was recalled to fill the post of supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kangxi he was recalled as supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏言：「四川、湖廣諸省官吏，借殿工採木，搜取民間屋材、墓樹，宜申飭禁止。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized: "In Sichuan, Huguang, and other provinces officials, under pretext of palace construction timber procurement, seize common people's house timber and tomb trees—order strict prohibition."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he reported that officials in Sichuan, Huguang, and elsewhere, under pretext of timber for palace construction, were seizing house beams and trees from ancestral graves, and called for strict prohibition.

sentences.zh: 又言：「採買官物，其由官發價者，如有駁減餘銀，例貯司庫。

translations.literal: He also said: "In purchasing official goods, where the price is issued by the government, if there is surplus silver from rejection or reduction, it is stored by rule in the department treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that when the government paid for official purchases, any surplus silver from rejected or reduced orders was supposed to go to the department treasury.

sentences.zh: 若價出自民，餘銀宜還之民間。」

translations.literal: If the price comes from the people, surplus silver should be returned to the people."
translations.idiomatic: But when the people paid, any surplus should be returned to them."

sentences.zh: 又言：「案牘煩冗滋弊，一部可迳結之事，即應一部迳結；

translations.literal: He also said: "Papers and dossiers grow redundant and breed abuse; matters one ministry can conclude directly should be concluded by one ministry;
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that redundant paperwork bred corruption: matters one ministry could settle should be settled by that ministry alone;

sentences.zh: 一疏可通結之事，即應一疏通結。

translations.literal: matters one memorial can conclude through should be concluded through in one memorial.
translations.idiomatic: and matters one memorial could close should be closed in one memorial.

sentences.zh: 若各省錢糧考成已報完者，部臣宜於議覆時即予開復。」

translations.literal: Where each province's tax and grain performance assessments have already reported completion, ministry officials should grant release at the time of deliberation and reply."
translations.idiomatic: Where a province had already reported its tax and grain accounts complete, the ministry should clear the record when replying to the memorial."

sentences.zh: 均如所請。

translations.literal: All were granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved as he had asked.

sentences.zh: 九年，考滿內升，命以正四品頂帶食俸任事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, on internal promotion after term assessment, he was ordered to wear rank-four insignia and draw salary while serving.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, after his term assessment and internal promotion, he was ordered to wear fourth-rank insignia, draw salary, and remain in office.

sentences.zh: 故事，給事中內升，還籍候補。

translations.literal: By precedent, supervising secretaries promoted internally returned to their native place to await supplementary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, a supervising secretary promoted internally returned home to await a new posting.

sentences.zh: 留任自文然始。

translations.literal: Remaining in office began with Wenran.
translations.idiomatic: Wenran was the first allowed to stay in post.

sentences.zh: 文然與魏象樞皆以給事中敢言負清望，號「姚魏」。

translations.literal: Wenran and Wei Xiangshu were both supervising secretaries famed for daring speech and clean reputation, called "Yao and Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Wenran and Wei Xiangshu were both outspoken supervising secretaries of spotless reputation, known together as "Yao and Wei."

sentences.zh: 十年，兩江總督麻勒吉坐事逮詣京師，仍用鎖系例。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Liangjiang Governor-General Maleji was arrested for an offense and taken to the capital, still under the shackling precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Liangjiang governor-general Maleji was arrested and brought to the capital in chains, following the usual practice.

sentences.zh: 文然复上疏論之，上諭：「自後命官赴質，概免鎖系，著為令。」

translations.literal: Wenran again memorialized on this; the Emperor instructed: "Henceforth when officials are summoned to answer charges, shackling is universally waived—establish this as an ordinance."
translations.idiomatic: Wenran memorialized again; the emperor ruled: "From now on officials summoned to answer charges shall not be shackled—make this a standing rule."

sentences.zh: 尋遷副都御史，再遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief, then again to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice censor-in-chief, then vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十二年，調兵部督捕侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of War in charge of bandit suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred to vice minister of war in charge of bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 京口副都統張所養劾將軍柯永蓁徇私縱恣，令文然往按，永蓁坐罷。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhang Suoyang memorialized that General Ke Yongzhen showed favoritism and indulgence; Wenran was sent to investigate, and Yongzhen was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suoyang, deputy commander at Jingkou, accused General Ke Yongzhen of favoritism and abuse; Wenran was sent to investigate and Yongzhen was removed.

sentences.zh: 遷左都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，疏言：「福建耿精忠、廣西孫延齡皆叛應吳三桂，中間阻隔，賴有廣東。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized: "Fujian's Geng Jingzhong and Guangxi's Sun Yanling both rebelled in answer to Wu Sangui; blocked in between, Guangdong was relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he wrote that Geng Jingzhong in Fujian and Sun Yanling in Guangxi had both joined Wu Sangui's rebellion, and that Guangdong alone stood between them.

sentences.zh: 精忠將士舊駐其地，熟習山川形勢，倘與延齡合謀相犄角，則廣東勢危。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's officers and men were long stationed there and know the mountains and rivers; if they join plots with Yanling in mutual support, Guangdong's situation would be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's troops had long been stationed there and knew the terrain; if they joined Yanling in a pincer, Guangdong would be in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 江西境與福建、廣東接，倘侵據贛州南安，驛道中斷，餉阻郵梗。

translations.literal: Jiangxi's border meets Fujian and Guangdong; if they seize and hold Ganzhou and Nan'an, courier routes would be cut and provisions and post blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi bordered both provinces; if rebels seized Ganzhou and Nan'an, courier routes would be cut and supplies and dispatches would be blocked.

sentences.zh: 宜駐重兵通聲援。」

translations.literal: Heavy troops should be stationed to maintain communication and support."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy forces should be posted there to keep lines of communication and support open."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 陝西提督王輔臣叛，河南巡撫佟鳳彩引疾，上已許之；

translations.literal: Shaanxi provincial commander-in-chief Wang Fuchen rebelled; Henan grand coordinator Tong Fengcai cited illness [to retire]; the Emperor had already permitted it;
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi commander Wang Fuchen rebelled, Henan grand coordinator Tong Fengcai pleaded illness to retire, and the emperor had already granted it;

sentences.zh: 文然言河南近陝西，流言方甚，鳳彩得民心，宜令力疾視事，上為留鳳彩。

translations.literal: Wenran said that Henan lies close to Shaanxi, that rumors were then running very strong, and that Fengcai enjoyed the people's hearts; he ought to be ordered to force himself through illness to attend to his duties—and on this account the Emperor kept Fengcai in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wenran argued that Henan bordered Shaanxi at a moment when rumors were spreading fast, and that Fengcai still commanded the people's trust; he should be ordered to take up his post despite illness. The Emperor accordingly retained Fengcai in his position.

sentences.zh: 文然屢有論列，尤推本君身，請節慎起居。

translations.literal: Wenran repeatedly submitted memorials on public affairs, above all tracing problems back to the ruler's own person, and asked that he be restrained and careful in his daily life.
translations.idiomatic: Wenran memorialized again and again on matters of state, always tracing the root of trouble back to the sovereign himself, and urged the Emperor to watch his conduct and live with greater restraint.

sentences.zh: 孝誠皇后崩，權攢鞏華城，上數臨視，文然密疏諫，且引唐太宗作台望昭陵用魏徵諫毀台事相擬，上亦受之，不怫也。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiaocheng died, the coffin was temporarily kept at Gonghua City; the Emperor went repeatedly to visit it. Wenran submitted a secret memorial of remonstrance, and cited in parallel Tang Taizong's building of a terrace to gaze upon Zhaoling and Wei Zheng's remonstrance to have the terrace destroyed. The Emperor accepted it and took no offense.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Xiaocheng's death, her coffin was temporarily kept at Gonghua City, and the Emperor visited it again and again. Wenran sent in a confidential memorial of remonstrance, comparing the situation to Tang Taizong's terrace built to view Zhaoling and Wei Zheng's counsel to tear it down. The Emperor took the advice without resentment.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時方更定條例，文然曰：「刃殺人一時，例殺人萬世，可無慎乎？」

translations.literal: Regulations were then being revised, and Wenran said: "A blade kills a man for a moment; a legal precedent kills men for ten thousand generations—can one not be cautious?"
translations.idiomatic: While new legal regulations were being drafted, Wenran said, "A knife may kill for an instant, but a precedent can condemn people for ten thousand generations—is that not reason enough for caution?"

sentences.zh: 乃推明律意，鉤稽揅討，必劑於寬平，決獄有所平反，歸輒色喜。

translations.literal: Thereupon he elucidated the intent of the law, scrutinized and examined cases, and always aimed at leniency and fairness; whenever a judgment was reversed on appeal, he would return home with a joyful look on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He then worked to clarify the meaning of the statutes, combing through cases with care and always steering toward leniency and equity. Whenever a wrongful conviction was overturned, he would go home beaming with satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 嘗疑獄有枉，爭之不得，退，長跪自責。

translations.literal: Once, suspecting that a case involved a wrongful conviction, he argued but could not prevail; upon retiring, he knelt for a long time in self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, convinced that a case had been wrongly decided, he argued his view in vain; when he withdrew, he knelt for a long time in bitter self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 又以明季用刑慘酷，奏除廷杖及鎮撫司諸非刑。

translations.literal: Citing also the cruel punishments of the late Ming, he memorialized to abolish court flogging and the various extralegal tortures of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also pointed to the brutal punishments of the late Ming and memorialized for the abolition of court flogging and the assorted illegal tortures practiced by the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，賜祭葬，諡端恪。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died; funeral rites were bestowed, and he was given the posthumous name Duankai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died. The court granted him funeral honors and the posthumous name Duankai, Upright and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 文然清介，里居幾不能自給，在官屏絕餽遺，晚益深研性命之學。

translations.literal: Wenran was upright and incorruptible; at home he could scarcely support himself, and in office he shut out all gifts and favors. In his later years he devoted himself ever more deeply to the study of human nature and destiny.
translations.idiomatic: Wenran was austere and incorruptible. In private life he could barely make ends meet; in office he refused every gift. In his later years he immersed himself ever more deeply in the moral philosophy of human nature and cosmic principle.

sentences.zh: 子士基，官湖廣羅田知縣；

translations.literal: His son Shiji served as magistrate of Luotian in Huguang;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiji served as magistrate of Luotian in Huguang;

sentences.zh: 士苾，官陝西朝邑知縣：皆有治行。

translations.literal: Shibi served as magistrate of Chaoyi in Shaanxi: both had records of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi served as magistrate of Chaoyi in Shaanxi—both sons were known for their able administration.

sentences.zh: 魏象樞，字環極，山西蔚州人。

translations.literal: Wei Xiangshu, styled Huanji, was a native of Weizhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiangshu, styled Huanji, was a native of Weizhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 四年，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「明季大弊未禁革者，督、撫、按聽用官舍太雜，道、府、州、縣胥隸太濫，請嚴予清釐。」

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "Among the great abuses of the late Ming not yet forbidden and abolished are these: governors-general, governors, and provincial censors employ official residences too indiscriminately, and clerks and runners at the circuit, prefectural, and county levels are too numerous—please impose strict rectification."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, "The late Ming left major abuses still unreformed: governors-general, governors, and provincial censors keep far too mixed a household of staff, while clerks and runners at every level from circuit down to county are far too many. I ask that these be rigorously cleaned up."

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，劾安徽巡撫王懩受賕庇貪吏，懩坐罷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he impeached Wang Yan, Governor of Anhui, for accepting bribes and shielding corrupt officials; Wang was dismissed as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he impeached Wang Yan, governor of Anhui, for taking bribes and protecting corrupt officials. Wang was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 轉工科右給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Works.

sentences.zh: 時以滿、漢雜處不便，令商民徙居南城。

translations.literal: At the time, because mixed Manchu and Han residence was considered inconvenient, merchants and commoners were ordered to move to the Southern City.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, mixed Manchu-Han residence was deemed inconvenient, and merchants and townspeople were ordered to relocate to the Southern City.

sentences.zh: 象樞疏言：「南城地狹，商民賃買無房，拆蓋無地。

translations.literal: Xiangshu memorialized: "The Southern City is cramped; merchants and commoners have no houses to rent or buy, and no land on which to demolish and rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshu memorialized, "The Southern City is too cramped. Merchants and townspeople can find no houses to rent or buy, and no space even to tear down old buildings and rebuild.

sentences.zh: 請下部察官地官房，俾民輸銀承業。」

translations.literal: Please order the ministries to inspect government land and government buildings, and allow the people to pay silver to take them over for their livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ministries survey government land and official buildings and allow the people to pay silver to take them over for their livelihood."

sentences.zh: 复疏請更定會典。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting a revision of the Collected Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial asking that the Collected Statutes be revised.

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: Both were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉刑科左給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to Left Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Left Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 八年，世祖親政，有司有以私徵侵帑坐罪者，象樞疏陳其弊，請飭州縣依易知單造格眼冊，註明人戶姓名、糧銀、款目及蠲賑清數，上大吏覈驗，印發開徵；

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when the Shizu Emperor personally assumed power, some officials were punished for unauthorized levies that encroached upon the treasury. Xiangshu memorialized detailing these abuses, and asked that prefectures and counties be ordered to compile ledger books following the simple notification format, recording household names, grain and silver amounts, item categories, and figures for tax exemptions and relief grants, to be verified by superior officials, stamped, and then used to begin collection;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the Shunzhi emperor took personal control of the government, some officials were punished for unauthorized levies that drained the public coffers. Xiangshu memorialized on these abuses and asked that prefectures and counties be required to compile ledger books in the simple notification format, listing household names, grain and silver quotas, item categories, and figures for exemptions and relief. These were to be checked by higher officials, stamped, and only then used to open collection.

sentences.zh: 又請定布政使會計之法，以杜欺隱，立內外各官治事之限，以清稽滯：皆見施行。

translations.literal: He also asked that accounting methods for provincial treasurers be fixed to stop fraud and concealment, and that time limits be set for all officials, internal and external, to clear backlogs: all of these were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed fixed accounting rules for provincial treasurers to prevent fraud, and deadlines for officials at every level to clear stalled business. All of these measures were adopted.

sentences.zh: 复疏言：「聖政方新，機務孔多，中外相望治平，非同昔日。

translations.literal: He again memorialized: "Sacred governance is newly underway, state affairs are numerous, and within and without all look toward peace and good order—it is not as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "A new reign has begun, state business is heavy, and everyone inside and outside the court looks to the promise of peace and order. This is not the world we knew before.

sentences.zh: 上近巡京畿，輔臣當陪侍法從，盡啟沃之忠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has recently toured the capital region; assisting ministers should accompany you in the imperial retinue and fully discharge their duty of counsel and nourishment.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has lately toured the capital region. Your chief ministers should accompany the imperial procession and give you their fullest counsel.

sentences.zh: 倘遠有臨幸，亦宜諫止鑾輿，副保傅之責。」

translations.literal: If there should be distant imperial progresses, they should also remonstrate to restrain the imperial carriage, fulfilling their responsibility as protectors and tutors."
translations.idiomatic: Should Your Majesty contemplate distant tours, they should also remonstrate to hold back the imperial carriage, in fulfillment of their duty as guardians and mentors of the throne."

sentences.zh: 又因災變上言，謂天地之變，乃人事反常所致。

translations.literal: Because of natural calamities he also submitted a memorial, stating that changes in Heaven and Earth are caused by human affairs gone awry.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial in response to natural disasters, arguing that disturbances in Heaven and Earth arise from human conduct gone wrong.

sentences.zh: 語侵權貴尤急。

translations.literal: His language in implicating the powerful and noble was especially pointed.
translations.idiomatic: His words were especially sharp where they touched the powerful and the well-connected.

sentences.zh: 九年，轉吏科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十年，大計，疏請復糾拾舊制，言官糾拾未得當，不宜反坐，下所司，著為令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, during the grand assessment, he memorialized requesting restoration of the old system for impeachment: when censorial officials impeach incorrectly, they should not be punished in return. This was referred to the relevant offices and established as a regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, at the grand assessment, he memorialized to restore the old impeachment rules: when a censor's accusation misses the mark, the accuser should not be punished in turn. The proposal was sent to the proper offices and made law.

sentences.zh: 因復疏言順治四年吏科左給事劉楗以糾拾被譴，宜予昭雪，上為復楗官。

translations.literal: He further memorialized that Liu Jian, Left Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel in the fourth year of Shunzhi, had been punished for impeachment and deserved exoneration; the Emperor restored Liu's office for him.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that Liu Jian, Left Supervising Secretary of the Bureau of Personnel in the fourth year of Shunzhi, had been punished for an impeachment and deserved to be cleared; the Emperor restored Liu to office.

sentences.zh: 總兵任珍失職怨望，​​並擅殺其家人，下九卿科道議罪，大學士陳名夏等二十八人，別為一議，象樞與焉。

translations.literal: The military commander Ren Zhen, resentful over dereliction of duty, also killed members of his household without authorization. The case was referred to the Nine Ministers and censorial officials for judgment; Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia and twenty-seven others submitted a separate opinion, and Xiangshu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander Ren Zhen, embittered by charges of dereliction, had also killed members of his own household on his own authority. The case was sent to the Nine Ministers and the censorial corps for judgment. Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia and twenty-seven others filed a separate opinion—and Xiangshu was one of them.

sentences.zh: 上責其徇黨負恩，下部議，罪應流，寬之，命留任。

translations.literal: The Emperor accused them of favoring their faction and betraying his grace; the case was referred to the ministry for deliberation. The crime warranted exile, but mercy was shown and they were ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked them for factional favoritism and ingratitude. The matter was referred to the ministry for judgment; the penalty should have been exile, but they were spared and ordered to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士寧完我劾名夏，辭連象樞，謂象樞與名夏姻家牛射鬥有連，象樞糾劾有誤，吏部議降級，名夏改票罰俸，命逮問。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Grand Secretary Ning Wanwo impeached Mingxia and implicated Xiangshu in the charge, alleging that Xiangshu was connected through marriage with Mingxia's relative Niu Shedou and that Xiangshu's impeachment had been mistaken. The Board of Civil Appointments recommended demotion; Mingxia was changed by imperial rescript to a fine of salary, and he was ordered seized for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Grand Secretary Ning Wanwo impeached Chen Mingxia and dragged Xiangshu into the case, claiming that Xiangshu was linked by marriage to Mingxia's kinsman Niu Shedou and that Xiangshu's impeachment had been wrong. The Board of Civil Appointments recommended demotion for Xiangshu; Mingxia, by imperial rescript, was reduced to a salary fine and ordered seized for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 象樞自陳素不識射鬥，得免議。

translations.literal: Xiangshu stated in his own defense that he had never known Shedou, and was exempted from the proposed punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshu declared in his own defense that he had never even known Niu Shedou, and was spared the proposed penalty.

sentences.zh: 尋以名夏父子濟惡，言官不先事論劾，各科都給事中皆鐫秩，象樞降補詹事府主簿，稍遷光祿寺丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the Mingxia father and son abetted each other's evil and censorial officials had not impeached them beforehand, all chief supervising secretaries of the various bureaus had their ranks reduced; Xiangshu was demoted and appointed chief clerk of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, then gradually promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, because the Mingxia father and son had abetted one another's wrongdoing and the censorial officials had failed to impeach them in time, every chief supervising secretary in the six bureaus had his rank cut. Xiangshu was demoted to chief clerk in the Household of the Heir Apparent, then gradually rose again to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以母老乞終養。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, citing his mother's age, he requested leave to care for her until her death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, with his mother advanced in years, he asked to retire and care for her until the end of her life.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，母喪終，用大學士馮溥薦，授貴州道御史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, when mourning for his mother was complete, on the recommendation of Grand Secretary Feng Pu he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Guizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, after his mourning period ended, he was appointed investigating censor for the Guizhou circuit on the recommendation of Grand Secretary Feng Pu.

sentences.zh: 入對，退而喜曰：「聖主在上，太平之業方始。

translations.literal: After an audience, upon retiring he said with joy: "A sage sovereign is on the throne; the enterprise of great peace is only beginning.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience with the throne, he withdrew in high spirits and said, "A sage ruler sits above us, and the work of building a lasting peace has only just begun.

sentences.zh: 不當以姑且補苴之言進。」

translations.literal: One should not submit merely provisional, stopgap words."
translations.idiomatic: This is no time to offer makeshift, patchwork counsel."

sentences.zh: 乃分疏，言：「王道首教化，滿、漢臣僚宜敦家教。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted separate memorials, stating: "The kingly way begins with moral transformation; Manchu and Han officials alike should earnestly cultivate family instruction."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a series of separate memorials. One said, "The kingly way begins with moral transformation; Manchu and Han officials alike should take family instruction seriously."

sentences.zh: 「督撫任最重，有不容不盡之職分、不容不去之因循，宜責成互糾。」

translations.literal: The responsibilities of governors-general and governors are weightiest; there are duties that brook no neglect and inertia that brooks no tolerance—they should be held accountable through mutual oversight."
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "The burden on governors-general and governors is greatest. There are duties that cannot be left undone and habits of delay that cannot be tolerated; they should be made to answer for one another through mutual oversight."

sentences.zh: 「制祿所以養廉，今罰俸例太嚴密，宜以記過示罰，增秩示恩。」

translations.literal: Regulated salaries exist to nurture integrity; the current regulations on salary fines are too stringent—demerits should serve to show punishment, and rank advancement to show favor."
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "Salaries are meant to sustain integrity, yet the rules for salary fines are now too harsh. Demerits should mark punishment, and promotions should mark reward."

sentences.zh: 「治河方亟，宜蓄人才備任使。」

translations.literal: River control is urgent; talent should be gathered in reserve for appointment and deployment."
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "River works are urgent; the state should stockpile capable men against the day they are needed."

sentences.zh: 「戒淫侈宜正人心，勵風俗宜修禮制。」

translations.literal: To guard against extravagance and excess, hearts must be set right; to encourage proper custom, ritual institutions should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Another said, "To curb extravagance, hearts must be set right; to strengthen public morals, ritual institutions must be restored."

sentences.zh: 聖祖多予褒納。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor largely praised and accepted these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor praised most of these proposals and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 复疏糾湖南布政使劉顯貴侵公帑不當內升，給事中餘司仁欺罔不法，皆坐黜。

translations.literal: Again he memorialized to impeach Hunan provincial administration commissioner Liu Xiangui for embezzling public funds and being improperly promoted internally, and supervising secretary Yu Siren for deceit and unlawful conduct; all were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He followed with another memorial impeaching Liu Xiangui, provincial administration commissioner of Hunan, for embezzling public funds and receiving an improper internal promotion, and Yu Siren, a supervising secretary, for fraud and misconduct; all were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以歲滿加四品卿銜，尋擢左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when his term was complete he received the additional title of fourth-rank grand secretary; soon he was promoted to Left Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after his term assessment, he received the additional title of fourth-rank grand secretary and was soon promoted to left assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，歲三遷，至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted three times within the year, reaching Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted three times in a single year, rising to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 會西南用兵，措兵食，察帑藏，多所規畫。

translations.literal: At that time the southwest was at war; he arranged military provisions, inspected treasury stores, and made many plans.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in the southwest, he organized military supplies, inspected treasury stores, and drew up many plans.

sentences.zh: 疏論籌餉，請確估價直，嚴覈關稅，慎用各直省布政使。

translations.literal: In a memorial on organizing supplies he asked for accurate price assessment, strict verification of customs duties, and careful use of provincial administration commissioners of the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial on provisioning he called for accurate price estimates, strict verification of customs duties, and careful selection of provincial administration commissioners.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「國家根本在百姓，百姓安危在督撫。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The foundation of the state lies in the people, and the people's safety and peril lie in the governors and governors-general.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The state's foundation is the people, and the people's welfare depends on the governors and governors-general.

sentences.zh: 原諸臣為百姓留膏血，為國家培元氣。

translations.literal: I hope the officials will preserve the people's lifeblood for the people and cultivate the state's vital energy for the state.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that officials preserve the people's substance and nurture the nation's vital strength.

sentences.zh: 臣不敢不為朝廷正紀綱，為臣子勵名節。」

translations.literal: Your servant dares not fail to set right discipline for the court and uphold integrity as a minister."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not fail to uphold discipline for the court and integrity as a minister."

sentences.zh: 因上申明憲綱十事，上嘉其切中時弊。

translations.literal: He then submitted ten items clarifying the censorial code; the Emperor praised them for hitting the abuses of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted ten points clarifying the censorial code, and the emperor praised them for striking at the abuses of the day.

sentences.zh: 各直省舉劾屬吏多失當，江蘇嘉定知縣陸隴其有清名而被劾罷，象樞疏薦之。

translations.literal: Recommendations and impeachments of subordinate officials in the provinces were often improper; Lu Longqi, magistrate of Jiading in Jiangsu, had a clean reputation yet was impeached and dismissed—Xiangshu memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial recommendations and impeachments of subordinates were often mishandled; Lu Longqi, magistrate of Jiading in Jiangsu, had a spotless reputation yet was impeached and removed—Xiangshu memorialized in his favor.

sentences.zh: 鎮江知府劉鼎溺職，題升糧道；

translations.literal: Liu Ding, prefect of Zhenjiang, neglected his duties, yet was nominated for promotion to grain intendant;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ding, prefect of Zhenjiang, had neglected his duties, yet was nominated for promotion as grain commissioner;

sentences.zh: 山西絳州知州曹廷俞劣跡顯著，糾察不及：象樞疏劾之。

translations.literal: Cao Tingyu, magistrate of Jiangzhou in Shanxi, had conspicuous misconduct that escaped investigation: Xiangshu memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Tingyu, magistrate of Jiangzhou in Shanxi, had conspicuous misconduct that had gone unchecked—Xiangshu memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 磨勘順天鄉試卷，因陳科場諸弊，請設內簾監試御史；

translations.literal: While reviewing Shuntian provincial examination papers, he set forth the abuses of the examination halls and asked that internal-curtain censors be appointed to supervise the exams;
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing the Shuntian provincial examination papers, he exposed examination abuses and asked that censors be posted inside the examination curtain to supervise the tests;

sentences.zh: 考核各直省學道，舉勞之辨、邵嘉，劾盧元培、程汝璞，上如其議以為黜陟。

translations.literal: Assessing provincial education commissioners of the provinces, he recommended Lao Zhibian and Shao Jia and impeached Lu Yuanpei and Cheng Rupu; the Emperor approved his recommendations for appointments and dismissals.
translations.idiomatic: In assessing provincial education commissioners, he recommended Lao Zhibian and Shao Jia and impeached Lu Yuanpei and Cheng Rupu; the emperor approved his recommendations for promotions and removals.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 象樞疏言：「臣忝司風紀，職多未盡，敢援漢臣汲黯自請為郎故事，留御史台，為朝廷整肅綱紀。」

translations.literal: Xiangshu memorialized: "Your servant disgracefully holds charge of discipline, yet has not fully fulfilled the duties; I venture to cite the Han precedent of Ji An asking to remain as an attendant, and to stay at the Censorate to rectify discipline for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshu memorialized: "I am charged with upholding discipline yet have not fully done my duty; I venture to cite the Han precedent of Ji An, who asked to remain in a lesser post, and request to stay at the censorate to restore the court's discipline."

sentences.zh: 上可其奏，以刑部尚書留左都御史任。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved the memorial and, though minister of justice, allowed him to retain the post of Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved; though appointed minister of justice, he was allowed to keep the post of left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 分疏劾山西巡撫王克善、榷稅蕪湖主事劉源諸不法狀，皆坐黜。

translations.literal: In separate memorials he impeached Shanxi Governor Wang Keshan and Liu Yuan, chief officer of the Wuhu transit customs, for various unlawful acts; all were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In separate memorials he impeached Shanxi governor Wang Keshan and Liu Yuan, chief officer at the Wuhu transit customs, for various unlawful acts; all were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 七月，地震，象樞與副都御史施維翰疏言：「地道，臣也。

translations.literal: In the seventh month there was an earthquake; Xiangshu and Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Weihan memorialized: "Earth has its way, and ministers are its embodiment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month an earthquake struck; Xiangshu and vice censor-in-chief Shi Weihan memorialized: "Earth corresponds to ministers.

sentences.zh: 臣失職，地為之不寧，請罪臣以回天變。」

translations.literal: Your servant has failed in duty, and the earth is unsettled on our account; please punish your servant to turn back the heavenly warning."
translations.idiomatic: We have failed in our duties, and the earth is unsettled because of us; please punish us to appease heaven's warning."

sentences.zh: 上召象樞入對，語移時，至泣下。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Xiangshu for audience; they spoke for a long while, until the Emperor wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xiangshu for a private audience; they spoke at length, until the emperor was in tears.

sentences.zh: 明日，上集廷臣於左翼門，詔極言大臣受賕徇私，會推不問操守；

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor assembled the court officials at Left Wing Gate and issued an edict strongly denouncing that grand ministers accept bribes and show favoritism, and that concurrent recommendations do not inquire into character;
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor assembled court officials at Left Wing Gate and issued an edict sharply condemning grand ministers who take bribes and show favoritism, and concurrent recommendations that ignore moral character;

sentences.zh: 將帥克敵，焚廬舍，俘子女，攘財物；

translations.literal: generals, on defeating the enemy, burn dwellings, capture women and children, and seize goods;
translations.idiomatic: generals who, after defeating the enemy, burn dwellings, capture women and children, and seize property;

sentences.zh: 外吏不言民生疾苦；

translations.literal: local officials do not speak of the people's hardships;
translations.idiomatic: local officials who say nothing of the people's hardships;

sentences.zh: 獄訟不以時結正；

translations.literal: lawsuits are not settled in timely fashion;
translations.idiomatic: lawsuits that are not promptly resolved;

sentences.zh: 諸王、貝勒、大臣家人罔市利，預詞訟：上乾天和，嚴飭修省。

translations.literal: princes, beile, and the households of grand ministers monopolize market profits and intervene in lawsuits: the Emperor said these offend heaven's harmony and ordered strict admonition and self-examination.
translations.idiomatic: princes, beile, and grand ministers' households who monopolize market profits and meddle in lawsuits—the emperor said these had offended heaven's harmony and ordered strict rectification and self-examination.

sentences.zh: 是時索額圖預政貪侈，詔多為索額圖發，論者謂象樞實啟之。

translations.literal: At that time Songgotu was wielding power with greed and extravagance; many edicts were aimed at Songgotu, and commentators said Xiangshu had actually set this in motion.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu was then wielding power with greed and extravagance; many edicts were directed at him, and commentators held that Xiangshu had actually sparked the campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋命舉廉吏，象樞舉原任侍郎雷虎、班迪、達哈塔、高珩，大理寺卿瑚密色，郎中宋文運，侍講蕭維豫，布政使畢振姬，知縣陸隴其、張沐凡十人。

translations.literal: Soon an order was issued to recommend honest officials; Xiangshu recommended ten men: former vice ministers Lei Hu, Badi, Dahaata, and Gao Heng; Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Humise; Director Song Wenyun; Hanlin Lecturer Xiao Weiyu; provincial administration commissioner Bi Zhenji; and magistrates Lu Longqi and Zhang Mu.
translations.idiomatic: An order soon went out to recommend honest officials; Xiangshu nominated ten men: former vice ministers Lei Hu, Badi, Dahaata, and Gao Heng; Chief Minister Humise of the Court of Judicial Review; Director Song Wenyun; Hanlin lecturer Xiao Weiyu; provincial administration commissioner Bi Zhenji; and magistrates Lu Longqi and Zhang Mu.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「雷虎朕亦聞其清，以其怠惰罷黜，既經象樞特薦，授內閣學士。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed: "Lei Hu—I too have heard of his integrity; he was dismissed for laziness; now that Xiangshu has specially recommended him, appoint him Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I too have heard Lei Hu is upright; he was dismissed for laziness, but since Xiangshu has specially recommended him, appoint him a grand secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 班迪清慎，因使往江西按事，未能明晰，問以民間苦樂，又謝不知，以是鐫秩。

translations.literal: Badi is clean and cautious; because he was sent to Jiangxi on an inspection, he could not give clear answers, and when asked about the people's hardships and joys he again pleaded ignorance—for this his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Badi is scrupulous and cautious, but when sent to Jiangxi on an inspection he could not give clear answers, and when asked about the people's hardships and joys he pleaded ignorance—for this his rank was reduced.

sentences.zh: 餘令吏部議奏錄用。」

translations.literal: As for the rest, order the Ministry of Personnel to discuss and memorialize on their appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ministry of Personnel discuss and recommend appointments for the rest."

sentences.zh: 十九年，仍授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was again appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 尋命與侍郎科爾坤巡察畿輔，按治豪猾，還奏稱旨。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered together with Vice Minister K'erkun to inspect the capital region, suppress the powerful and lawless, and on returning his report pleased the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered, together with Vice Minister K'erkun, to inspect the capital region and suppress powerful wrongdoers; his report on return pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 象樞有疾，上賜以人參及參膏，命內侍問飲食如何。

translations.literal: Xiangshu fell ill; the Emperor bestowed ginseng and ginseng paste and ordered eunuchs to ask how his food and drink were.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangshu fell ill, the emperor sent him ginseng and ginseng paste and ordered eunuchs to inquire after his meals.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，奏事乾清門，躓焉，即日疏乞休，再奏，乃許之，命之入對，賜御書寒松堂額，令馳驛歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, while reporting on business at Qianqing Gate he stumbled; that same day he memorialized requesting retirement; after a second memorial it was granted; he was ordered to audience, given an imperial inscription for the Hall of Cold Pines, and sent home by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he stumbled while reporting business at Qianqing Gate; that same day he memorialized to retire, and after a second memorial was permitted; he was summoned for audience, given an imperial plaque for the Hall of Cold Pines, and sent home by post relay.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，卒，年七十一，賜祭葬，諡敏果。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died, aged seventy-one; funeral sacrifices were granted and his posthumous title was Min'guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he died at seventy-one; funeral honors were granted and he was posthumously titled Min'guo.

sentences.zh: 象樞以馮溥薦再起。

translations.literal: Xiangshu was recalled to office on Feng Pu's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshu returned to office on Feng Pu's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 象樞見溥，問何以見知？

translations.literal: Xiangshu saw Pu and asked how he had come to know him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshu visited Pu and asked how he had come to be noticed.

sentences.zh: 溥曰：「昔餘為祭酒，故事，丁祭不得陪祀者，當於前一日瞻拜。

translations.literal: Pu said: "Formerly when I was Grand Examiner, by precedent those who could not attend the spring and autumn sacrificial rites were to pay reverence the day before.
translations.idiomatic: Pu said: "When I was grand examiner, the custom was that those who could not attend the spring and autumn sacrifices should pay reverence the day before.

sentences.zh: 君每期必至，敬慎成禮。

translations.literal: You came every time without fail, reverent and careful in completing the rite.
translations.idiomatic: You came every time without fail, reverent and careful in observing the rite.

sentences.zh: 一歲直大雨，君仍至，肅然瞻拜而去，此外無一人至者。

translations.literal: One year there was heavy rain, yet you still came, paid reverence solemnly and left; besides you, not one person came.
translations.idiomatic: One year it poured with rain, yet you still came, paid reverence solemnly, and left—no one else came at all.

sentences.zh: 餘以是知君篤誠。」

translations.literal: From this I knew your deep sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: From that I knew your deep sincerity."

sentences.zh: 子學誠，進士，授中書。

translations.literal: His son Xuecheng was a jinshi, appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuecheng passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 上推象樞恩，改編修，官至諭德。

translations.literal: The Emperor extended Xiangshu's favor to him, changed his appointment to Compiler, and he rose to the post of Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor extended Xiangshu's favor to him, transferred him to compiler, and he rose to lecturer.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶間，錄賢良祠諸臣後裔，賜象樞四世孫煜舉人。

translations.literal: During the Jiaqing period, when recording the descendants of worthies in the Shrine of Worthies, Xiangshu's fourth-generation descendant Yu was granted juren status.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign, when descendants of shrine worthies were recorded, Xiangshu's fourth-generation descendant Yu was granted juren status.

sentences.zh: 硃之弼，字右君，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhibi, style name Youjun, was a man of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhibi, whose style was Youjun, came from Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授禮科給事中，轉工科都給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Rites section and transferred to chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works section.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites and later became chief supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言：「國家宜重名器。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized: "The state should value official titles and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he memorialized: "The state should hold official titles and insignia in esteem.

sentences.zh: 舊制，胥吏供役年久無過，予以議敘，選用佐貳。

translations.literal: Under the old system, clerks who served for many years without fault were given consideration for promotion and selected for assistant deputy posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, clerks who had served many years without fault were considered for promotion and appointed to assistant deputy posts.

sentences.zh: 今戶、兵等部書役別系職銜，非官非吏，有玷班行。

translations.literal: Today in the Ministries of Revenue, War, and others, clerical runners hold titular ranks in a separate category—they are neither officials nor clerks—and this stains the order of ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the ministries of Revenue, War, and the like, clerical staff carry separate titular ranks—neither true officials nor proper clerks—and this debases the whole order of office.

sentences.zh: 此曹起自貧乏，不數年家貲鉅萬，衣食奢侈。

translations.literal: These men began in poverty; within a few years their household wealth reached tens of thousands, and their food and clothing are extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: They began in poverty; within a few years their households amassed fortunes of tens of thousands, and they live in extravagant luxury.

sentences.zh: 非舞文作姦，何以致此？

translations.literal: If not by twisting the law and committing fraud, how could they reach this?
translations.idiomatic: If they were not twisting the law and committing fraud, how else could they have come to this?

sentences.zh: 戶、兵堂司官歲有遷轉，此曹歷年久不去，官為客，吏為主，流弊何窮。

translations.literal: The department heads of Revenue and War rotate every year, yet these men remain year after year without leaving; officials are guests, clerks are masters—where do the abuses end?
translations.idiomatic: Department heads in Revenue and War rotate every year, yet these men stay on for years without leaving—officials are guests, clerks are masters—and the abuses know no end.

sentences.zh: 請嚴察褫奪。」

translations.literal: I request strict investigation and stripping of their posts."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be rigorously investigated and stripped of their posts."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was transmitted to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent down to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 九年，以父喪去。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he left office on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he left office to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 十一年，起補戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was recalled to fill the post of chief supervising secretary of the Revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled and appointed chief supervising secretary in the Revenue section.

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏言：「小民納糧一也，而其目有四：曰漕糧、白糧、軍糧、恤孤糧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized: "The common people pay grain tax as one obligation, yet its categories are four: transport grain, white grain, military grain, and orphan-relief grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he memorialized: "Ordinary people owe grain tax as a single obligation, yet it falls into four categories: canal transport grain, white grain, military grain, and orphan-relief grain.

sentences.zh: 軍糧、恤孤糧程限遲緩，無增耗之費，有力之家，往往營求撥兌；

translations.literal: Military grain and orphan-relief grain have lenient deadlines and no surcharge for wastage; wealthy households often maneuver to have their obligations reassigned;
translations.idiomatic: Military grain and orphan-relief grain carry slow deadlines and no surcharge for wastage, so wealthy households often maneuver to have their obligations reassigned elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 單弱之戶，派納漕、白，苦樂不均。

translations.literal: weak and solitary households are assigned transport grain and white grain—hardship and ease are not equally shared.
translations.idiomatic: while weak and solitary households are assigned transport grain and white grain, so that hardship and ease are not equally borne.

sentences.zh: 軍糧行折色，軍得銀則妄費，生掛欠之弊。

translations.literal: When military grain is commuted to silver, soldiers who receive silver spend it recklessly, producing the abuse of arrears on the books.
translations.idiomatic: When military grain is commuted to silver, soldiers who receive the cash spend it recklessly, giving rise to the abuse of paper arrears.

sentences.zh: 恤孤糧半飽豪強，鰥寡孤獨無由控訴。

translations.literal: Orphan-relief grain half feeds the powerful; widows, orphans, and the solitary have no means to complain.
translations.idiomatic: Orphan-relief grain half fills the bellies of the powerful, while widows, orphans, and the utterly alone have no way to lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 請飭漕臣下各省糧道，親督州縣畫一編徵，盡數輸納，敢有撥兌者治罪。」

translations.literal: Please order transport officials and grain intendants in each province to personally supervise prefectures and counties in uniform compilation and collection, deliver the full amounts, and punish any who dare to seek reassignment."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that transport officials and provincial grain intendants be ordered to supervise prefectures and counties personally in uniform registration and collection, deliver the full amounts, and punish anyone who dares seek reassignment."

sentences.zh: 又言：「錢糧侵欠，兵食不充，為上所廑念。

translations.literal: He also said: "Embezzlement and arrears in taxes and grain, and insufficient military provisions, are matters the emperor deeply cares about.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Embezzlement and arrears in taxes and grain, and the failure to fill military rations, are matters that weigh heavily on the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 侵欠之大者，曰漕欠、糧欠。

translations.literal: The largest embezzlements and arrears are called transport arrears and grain arrears.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest embezzlements and arrears are transport arrears and grain arrears.

sentences.zh: 漕欠責漕督親督糧道，糧欠責督撫親督布政使，令本年附徵。

translations.literal: Transport arrears should be the responsibility of transport commissioners who personally supervise grain intendants; grain arrears should be the responsibility of governors who personally supervise provincial treasurers—order supplementary collection in the current year.
translations.idiomatic: Transport arrears should be the responsibility of transport commissioners, who must personally oversee grain intendants; grain arrears should be the responsibility of governors-general and governors, who must personally oversee provincial treasurers—with orders to collect the shortfall additionally in the current year.

sentences.zh: 某年欠項逾限不完，以溺職論，有司侵虧怠緩，糾劾不貸。

translations.literal: If any year's arrears are not cleared within the deadline, consider it dereliction of duty; officials who embezzle, squander, or delay should be impeached without leniency.
translations.idiomatic: If any year's arrears are not cleared within the deadline, treat it as dereliction of duty; officials who embezzle, squander, or drag their feet should be impeached without mercy.

sentences.zh: 如此，則年銷年欠，宿逋可清。」
