translations.literal: Thus year by year arrears would be cleared, and long-standing debts could be settled."
translations.idiomatic: In this way each year's arrears would be cleared as it came due, and long-standing debts could at last be settled."

sentences.zh: 上韙其言，並嚴飭行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and sternly ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice and sternly ordered that it be carried out.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「國家章制大備，部臣實心任事，利自知舉，弊自知革。

translations.literal: He memorialized again: "The state's statutes and regulations are fully in place; if ministry officials sincerely attend to their duties, benefits they would know to advance and abuses they would know to reform.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "The state's statutes and regulations are complete; if ministry officials truly applied themselves to their duties, they would know which benefits to advance and which abuses to remove.

sentences.zh: 今乃盡若事外，遇事至，才者不肯決，無才者不能決，稍重大即請會議。

translations.literal: Now they all act as if matters were none of their business; when business arrives, the capable will not decide, the incapable cannot decide, and anything slightly important they request joint consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Now they all behave as though affairs were none of their concern: when business arrives, the capable refuse to decide, the incapable cannot decide, and anything even slightly weighty is referred for joint consultation.

sentences.zh: 不然，行外察報，遷延歲月而已；

translations.literal: Otherwise they send out external inspection reports and delay for months on end;
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they dispatch external inspection reports and let matters drag on for months;

sentences.zh: 不然，聽督撫參奏，科道指糾而已；

translations.literal: otherwise they let governors memorialize impeachments and censorial officials point out faults—nothing more;
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they leave it to governors to memorialize impeachments and censorial officials to lodge accusations—and nothing more;

sentences.zh: 不然，苟且塞責，無容再議而已：上下相諉，彼此相安。

translations.literal: otherwise they perfunctorily fulfill the minimum and allow no further discussion: superiors and subordinates shift blame, and each finds comfort in the status quo.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise they perfunctorily check a box and allow no further discussion: superiors and subordinates shift blame onto one another, and each settles comfortably into the status quo.

sentences.zh: 國家事安得不廢，百姓安得不困？

translations.literal: How could state affairs fail to decay? How could the people fail to suffer?
translations.idiomatic: How could state affairs fail to fall into ruin? How could the people fail to be driven to distress?

sentences.zh: 欲致太平，必無之事也。

translations.literal: To seek peace and order—this would necessarily be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of bringing about peace and good order would be to chase an impossibility.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂今日求治，首在擇人。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly considers that in seeking good governance today, selecting men comes first.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly believes that in seeking good government today, the first task is to choose the right men.

sentences.zh: 上面召諸大臣親試才品​​，因能授任；

translations.literal: Let Your Majesty summon senior ministers to test their talent and character in person and assign posts according to ability;
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty summon the senior ministers to test their talent and character in person, and assign posts according to ability;

sentences.zh: 复考其歷事後興利幾何，除弊幾何，定功罪，信賞罰，則法行而事舉矣。」

translations.literal: then examine how much benefit they brought and how much abuse they removed after serving—fix merit and guilt, keep rewards and punishments trustworthy—and then laws will be enforced and affairs accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: then review how much benefit they brought and how much abuse they removed in office—fix merit and guilt, make rewards and punishments trustworthy—and law will be enforced and affairs will be accomplished."

sentences.zh: 上納之弼言，諭六部去怠忽舊習。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted Zhibi's advice and instructed the Six Ministries to cast off their old habits of negligence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Zhibi's counsel and instructed the Six Ministries to abandon their old habits of negligence.

sentences.zh: 一歲中四遷，授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Within one year he was transferred four times and was appointed vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single year he was transferred four times and was appointed vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年，河西務鈔關員外郎硃世德徵稅不如額，戶部援赦請免議，上切責譴部臣，之弼降三級。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhu Shide, assistant department director at the He Xi Wu transit toll station, collected taxes below quota; the Ministry of Revenue cited the amnesty to request exemption from deliberation; the emperor sharply rebuked and censured the ministry officials, and Zhibi was demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhu Shide, assistant department director at the He Xi Wu transit toll station, collected taxes below quota; the Ministry of Revenue cited the amnesty to ask that the case be exempted from deliberation; the emperor sharply rebuked and censured the ministry officials, and Zhibi was demoted three ranks.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授光祿寺少卿，再遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred again to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then promoted again to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「巡按未得其人，當責都察院考核，巡按之賢不肖，即都察院堂上官賢不肖。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "If touring censors are not the right men, the Censorate should be held accountable in evaluation; whether touring censors are worthy or unworthy reflects whether the Censorate's senior officials are worthy or unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When touring censors are not the right men, the Censorate itself should be held accountable in evaluation—for whether touring censors are worthy or unworthy reflects whether the Censorate's senior officials are worthy or unworthy.

sentences.zh: 臣與諸巡按約，操守當潔清，舉劾當得宜，撫按當互糾。

translations.literal: I have made agreements with touring censors that conduct should be pure, impeachment and recommendation should be fitting, and governors and censors should mutually impeach one another.
translations.idiomatic: I have bound the touring censors to an agreement: conduct must be pure, impeachment and recommendation must be fitting, and governors and censors must impeach one another.

sentences.zh: 臣等定差不公，考核不當，巡按賢者不薦，不肖者不糾，諸御史亦得論劾。

translations.literal: If we assign posts unfairly or evaluate improperly—if worthy touring censors are not recommended and unworthy ones are not impeached—other censors may also impeach us.
translations.idiomatic: If we assign posts unfairly or evaluate them improperly—if worthy touring censors go unrecommended and unworthy ones go unimpeached—the other censors may impeach us as well.

sentences.zh: 至巡方應行諸事，當令掌河南道會諸御史各抒見聞，奏請明定畫一。」

translations.literal: As for all matters that should be carried out on inspection tours, the head of the Henan circuit should convene the censors to set forth what each has observed, and memorialize requesting clear uniform regulations."
translations.idiomatic: As for all matters that should be carried out on provincial inspection tours, the head of the Henan circuit should convene the censors so that each may set forth what he has observed, and memorializing, request that clear uniform rules be established."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: His request was approved.

sentences.zh: 世祖惡貪吏，命官得贓十兩、役得贓一兩，皆流徙。

translations.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor hated corrupt officials and decreed that any official convicted of bribes of ten taels or any clerk of one tael would all be exiled.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi Emperor hated corrupt officials and decreed that any official found guilty of ten taels in bribes, or any clerk of one tael, would be exiled.

sentences.zh: 令既行，之弼疏論其不便，略謂：「自上諭宣傳後，撫按所糾，必無以大貪入告者。

translations.literal: Once the decree was in effect, Zhibi memorialized arguing its inconvenience, saying in summary: "Since the imperial edict was proclaimed and circulated, what governors and censors impeach will certainly never be large-scale corruption reported as such.
translations.idiomatic: Once the decree took effect, Zhibi memorialized against its drawbacks, saying in essence: "Since the imperial edict was proclaimed and circulated, what governors and censors impeach will never be reported as large-scale corruption.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 一經提問，有司無不圖保身命，雖盈千累百，而及其結讞，期不滿十兩而止。

translations.literal: Once formal interrogation begins, local officials invariably seek to preserve their lives; though the sums may be thousands accumulated over hundreds of cases, when the verdict is finalized they aim to stop short of ten taels.
translations.idiomatic: Once formal interrogation begins, local officials invariably seek to save their own lives; though the sums may run to thousands piled up over hundreds of cases, when the verdict is finalized they aim to stop just short of ten taels.

sentences.zh: 是未糾以前，徒層累而輸於大吏。

translations.literal: Thus before impeachment, bribes are merely passed layer by layer up to senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thus before impeachment ever occurs, bribes are simply passed up layer by layer to senior officials.

sentences.zh: 被糾之後，又層累而輸於問官。

translations.literal: After impeachment, they are passed layer by layer again to the interrogating officials.
translations.idiomatic: After impeachment, they are passed up layer by layer again to the interrogating officials.

sentences.zh: 尺籍所科，百不一二。

translations.literal: What is entered in the official records as charged is not one or two in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Of what is actually charged in the official records, scarcely one or two cases in a hundred reflect the truth.

sentences.zh: 蓋雖起龔、黃為今之有司，未有不犯十兩之令者。

translations.literal: For even if one raised Gong Yu and Huang Ba to serve as today's local officials, none would fail to run afoul of the ten-tael decree.
translations.idiomatic: For even if Gong Yu and Huang Ba themselves were raised up to serve as today's local officials, not one would fail to run afoul of the ten-tael decree.

sentences.zh: 而今普天之下，皆不取十兩之有司，豈真出古循吏上哉？

translations.literal: Yet now under heaven all local officials take no more than ten taels—could they truly surpass the exemplary officials of antiquity?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now under heaven every local official is said to take no more than ten taels—could they truly surpass the exemplary officials of antiquity?

sentences.zh: 良以令嚴則思遁，徒有名而無其實也。

translations.literal: Rather, when the law is strict men think to evade it—there is name only, without reality.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, when the law is strict men think only of evasion—the name remains, but the reality is gone.

sentences.zh: 上但擇撫按一大貪者懲之，一大廉者獎之，則眾貪懼、眾廉奮矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would simply select one grossly corrupt governor or censor and punish him, and one greatly upright and reward him, then the corrupt would fear and the upright would be emboldened."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty would simply choose one grossly corrupt governor or censor and punish him, and one greatly upright and reward him, then the corrupt would fear and the upright would take heart."

sentences.zh: 會歲旱求言，之弼疏言：「山東巡撫耿焞、河南巡撫賈漢復以墾荒蒙賞，兩省百姓即以賠熟受困，歲增數十萬賦稅，多得之於鞭笞敲剝、呼天搶地之孑遺。

translations.literal: When a drought occurred and the throne sought advice, Zhibi memorialized: "The governors of Shandong, Geng Tun, and Henan, Jia Hanfu, were rewarded for opening wasteland to cultivation, yet the people of both provinces were immediately burdened by compensation for land already under cultivation; taxes rose by hundreds of thousands each year, mostly wrung from bereft survivors through beating, extortion, and cries of anguish to heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought year, when the court solicited memorials, Zhibi wrote: "The governors of Shandong, Geng Tun, and Henan, Jia Hanfu, were rewarded for land reclamation, but the people of both provinces were at once crushed by compensation levies on fields already in cultivation. Annual taxes increased by hundreds of thousands of taels, most of it extracted by whip and squeeze from the last desperate survivors wailing to heaven and beating the ground in grief.

sentences.zh: 怨苦之氣，積為沴厲。」

translations.literal: The air of resentment and suffering accumulated into pestilence and calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Resentment and suffering piled up until they turned into pestilence and disaster."

sentences.zh: 又疏劾戶部賑濟需遲，救荒無術。

translations.literal: He also memorialized censuring the Ministry of Revenue for delay in famine relief and lack of any effective means of disaster relief.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial impeaching the Ministry of Revenue for sluggish famine relief and its failure to devise any real plan for saving people from starvation.

sentences.zh: 京師既得雨，河南報彰德、衛輝以旱成災，戶部奏：「上步禱天壇，時雨方降。

translations.literal: After the capital had already received rain, Henan reported that Zhangde and Weihui had suffered drought disaster. The Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "When Your Majesty walked in prayer at the Temple of Heaven, timely rain had just begun to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Once rain had already fallen in the capital, Henan reported drought disasters in Zhangde and Weihui. The Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "When Your Majesty walked in prayer at the Temple of Heaven, the timely rain had only just begun to fall.

sentences.zh: 彰德、衛輝地接畿南，何獨請蠲卹？

translations.literal: Zhangde and Weihui adjoin the southern capital region—why alone request remission and relief?
translations.idiomatic: Zhangde and Weihui lie close to the southern approaches of the capital—why should they alone seek tax remission and relief?

sentences.zh: 請覆勘。」

translations.literal: Request re-investigation."
translations.idiomatic: We request a fresh investigation."

sentences.zh: 之弼疏爭，略謂：「百里不同風，千里不同雨，安得以輦下例率土？

translations.literal: Zhibi memorialized in protest, saying in summary: "Within a hundred li customs differ; within a thousand li rains differ. How can the region under the imperial carriage be taken as the standard for the whole realm?
translations.idiomatic: Zhibi answered with a counter-memorial, arguing in essence: "Customs differ within a hundred li, and rain differs within a thousand. How can conditions at the capital be made the measure for the entire empire?

sentences.zh: 且以撫臣疏報為不可信，而又倚以覆勘，使撫臣告災如前，部臣信之不可，不信必易人而勘，徒使地方增煩擾耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, the governors' memorial reports are deemed untrustworthy, yet investigation is still relied upon—if governors report disaster as before, ministry officials cannot believe them, and if they disbelieve, officials must be replaced for investigation, only adding local harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the governors' reports are treated as unreliable, yet the ministry still insists on reinvestigation. If a governor reports disaster as before, the ministry can neither accept it nor reject it without sending someone else to verify the case—nothing is gained but fresh trouble for the locality.

sentences.zh: 自夏徂冬，被災州縣未盡停徵，待勘明已至來春，雖蠲免，徒飽吏橐，饑民轉為溝中瘠久矣。」

translations.literal: From summer through winter, disaster-affected prefectures and counties have not fully suspended collection; by the time verification is complete it will already be next spring, and even if remitted, it will only fill officials' purses while starving people have long since become bones in ditches."
translations.idiomatic: From summer to winter, stricken prefectures and counties still have not stopped collection in full. By the time the investigation is finished, spring will already be here. Even if remissions are granted then, they will only fill officials' pockets, while the starving will long since have become skeletons in the ditches."

sentences.zh: 與尚書王弘祚廷辨，卒從之弼議。

translations.literal: He debated in court with Minister Wang Hongzuo, and the emperor ultimately adopted Zhibi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He argued the matter before the throne with Minister Wang Hongzuo, and in the end the court sided with Zhibi.

sentences.zh: 十八年，复授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was again appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, he was again appointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kangxi, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷左都御史，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and elevated to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was made left censor-in-chief and promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏言：「福建官兵月米五十餘萬石，歲徵十萬餘石，餘皆糴諸市，石值銀二兩四錢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he memorialized: "Fujian's troops and officers require more than five hundred thousand shi of grain each month; only a little over one hundred thousand shi are levied annually, and the rest must be purchased in the market at two taels four mace of silver per shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, he memorialized: "Fujian's garrison requires more than five hundred thousand shi of grain each month. Only a little over one hundred thousand shi are raised by levy each year; the rest must be bought in the market at two taels and four mace per shi.

sentences.zh: 朝廷買米養兵，絕不抑值以累民。

translations.literal: When the court buys grain to feed troops, it must never suppress prices to burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the court buys grain to feed the army, it must never force prices down and thereby burden the people.

sentences.zh: 臣聞延、建、汀、邵諸府民以買米攤賠為累，有原繳田入官者。

translations.literal: I hear that in the prefectures of Yanping, Jianning, Tingzhou, and Shaowu the people are burdened by apportioned compensation for grain purchases, and some have had fields they originally paid taxes on confiscated by the government.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in Yanping, Jianning, Tingzhou, and Shaowu the people are crushed by apportioned surcharges for grain purchases, and some have even had fields on which they had long paid taxes seized by the government.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉之間，按地派米，石必加六斗，又迫令折價三四兩不等，數倍於正供，民不勝其朘削。」

translations.literal: Between Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, grain is allocated by land, with an additional six dou required per shi, and people are forced to pay commutation at three or four taels and more—several times the regular quota—so the people cannot bear the extortion."
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhangzhou and Quanzhou, grain is assigned by acreage, with six extra dou added to every shi, and people are then forced to commute the payment at three or four taels or more—several times the regular quota. The people cannot endure such bleeding."

sentences.zh: 上特諭督撫嚴察。

translations.literal: The emperor specially ordered the governors-general and governors to investigate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special edict ordering the governors-general and governors to investigate the matter rigorously.

sentences.zh: 七年，調刑部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏言：「各省存留錢糧，順治間軍需正迫，有裁減之令。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he memorialized: "Each province's retained funds and grain—in the Shunzhi reign, when military needs pressed urgently, there were orders to reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, he memorialized: "The retained funds and grain of each province—during the Shunzhi reign, when military expenses pressed hard, orders were issued to cut them back.

sentences.zh: 昨年部臣又請酌減。

translations.literal: Last year ministry officials again requested discretionary reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the ministry again asked that they be reduced further.

sentences.zh: 存留各款，原為留備地方公用，事不容已，費無所出，勢不得不派之民間，不肖有司因以為利。

translations.literal: The various retained categories were originally kept in reserve for local public use; when affairs cannot be avoided and expenses have nowhere to come from, the situation inevitably forces levy on the populace, and unworthy officials profit thereby.
translations.idiomatic: These retained items were originally set aside for local public needs. When business cannot be postponed and there is no other source of funds, officials have no choice but to levy the people—and corrupt ones turn that necessity into profit.

sentences.zh: 宜復康熙七年以前存留舊例。」

translations.literal: It is appropriate to restore the old retained-funds precedents from before the seventh year of Kangxi."
translations.idiomatic: The old retained-funds regulations in force before the seventh year of Kangxi should be restored."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「八旗家丁，每歲以自盡報部者不下二千人。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Among Eight Banner household bondservants, those reported to the ministry as having committed suicide each year are no fewer than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Among the household bondservants of the Eight Banners, no fewer than two thousand are reported each year to the ministry as having taken their own lives.

sentences.zh: 人雖有貴賤，均屬赤子。

translations.literal: Though people have high and low station, all are the emperor's children.
translations.idiomatic: High or low in station, they are all the emperor's own children.

sentences.zh: 請敕諭八旗，凡蓄僕婢，當時其教誨，足其衣食，卹其勞苦，減其鞭笞，使各得其所。

translations.literal: Request an imperial edict to the Eight Banners that whoever keeps servants should educate them in season, provide sufficient clothing and food, care for their labor and hardship, reduce beatings, and allow each to find their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Eight Banners be instructed by edict that all who keep servants and maids should instruct them properly, provide adequate food and clothing, show concern for their toil, lessen the lash, and let each person live as he ought.

sentences.zh: 歲終刑部列歲中自盡人數，系某旗某家，具冊呈覽，俾人知儆惕。」

translations.literal: At year's end the Ministry of Punishments should list the year's suicides, noting which banner and which household, submit a register for review, so people may know caution and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: At year's end the Ministry of Punishments should compile the year's suicides, record the banner and household involved, and submit the register for the emperor's review, so that all may take warning."

sentences.zh: 又言：「世祖嚴治貪官蠹役，特立嚴法，如非官役，不用此例。

translations.literal: He also said: "Emperor Shizu strictly punished corrupt officials and parasitic clerks and established stern law, which if one was not an official or clerk, did not apply.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Emperor Shizu dealt severely with corrupt officials and parasitic clerks and established harsh penalties, but those penalties were not meant to apply to persons who were neither officials nor clerks.

sentences.zh: 今不論有祿無祿，通用重典。

translations.literal: Now without distinction between those with salary and those without, heavy punishments are applied universally.
translations.idiomatic: Now, without distinguishing salaried officials from others, the heavy penalties are applied across the board.

sentences.zh: 貪蠹事發，被證畏同罪，刑訊不承，使大貪漏網。

translations.literal: When corruption cases arise, those implicated fear equal guilt, refuse confession under torture, and let the greater corrupt escape the net.
translations.idiomatic: When a case of graft comes to light, witnesses fear sharing the same punishment, resist confession under torture, and the greatest offenders slip through the net.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後因事納賄，仍擬同罪。

translations.literal: Request that hereafter those taking bribes in connection with affairs still be sentenced as accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter anyone who accepts a bribe in connection with an affair still be sentenced as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 如逼抑出錢，倘非官役，許用舊律。」

translations.literal: For coerced payment of money, if the person is not an official or clerk, allow application of the old statutes."
translations.idiomatic: But where money is extorted by coercion, if the extortionist is not an official or clerk, the old law should be allowed to apply."

sentences.zh: 詔並如所請。

translations.literal: An edict approved all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved every one of his requests.

sentences.zh: 九年，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, he was transferred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以母喪去官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he left office due to his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十七年，起授工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he was recalled and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, he was recalled to service and appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，會推湖北按察使，之弼舉道員王垓，不當上意，以所舉非材，吏部議降三級調用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, at a joint recommendation session for Hubei provincial surveillance commissioner, Zhibi recommended circuit intendant Wang Gai—not to the emperor's liking; for recommending an unqualified man, the Ministry of Personnel proposed demotion by three ranks and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, at a joint recommendation for the Hubei surveillance commissioner, Zhibi put forward circuit intendant Wang Gai. The choice displeased the emperor, and because the nominee was judged unfit, the Ministry of Personnel recommended demoting Zhibi three ranks and reassigning him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 之弼內行修篤，事親孝，與其弟之佐相友愛。

translations.literal: Zhibi was upright in personal conduct, filial in serving his parents, and affectionate with his younger brother Zhizuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibi was deeply principled in private life, filial toward his parents, and warmly devoted to his younger brother Zhizuo.

sentences.zh: 之佐，順治十四年進士，選庶吉士，歷官侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Zhizuo was a jinshi of the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, and served successively as reader-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizuo passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and rose to serve as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 嚴事之弼，雖白首，執子弟禮甚謹。

translations.literal: He revered Zhibi strictly; though white-haired, he observed the etiquette of a younger kinsman with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zhibi with the utmost respect; even in old age, he still observed toward his elder brother the careful deference of a junior kinsman.

sentences.zh: 趙申喬，字慎旃，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shenqiao, style name Shenzhan, was a man of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shenqiao, whose style was Shenzhan, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the ninth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授河南商丘知縣，有惠政。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was appointed magistrate of Shangqiu in Henan, with benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, he was appointed magistrate of Shangqiu in Henan, where his rule brought real benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，以賢能行取，命以主事用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was selected for promotion on merit and virtue and ordered appointed as principal secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, he was selected for capital office on account of merit and ability and appointed a principal secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, he was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 三十年，遷員外郎，以病乞歸。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, he was promoted to vice director and requested retirement due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, he was promoted to vice director, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 四十年，以直隸巡撫李光地薦，召見，上察申喬敬慎，超擢浙江布政使。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year, on recommendation of Zhili governor Li Guangdi, he was summoned for audience; the emperor observed Shenqiao's prudence and circumspection and promoted him directly to administration commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year, on the recommendation of Li Guangdi, governor of Zhili, he was summoned to audience. Seeing Shenqiao's sober diligence, the emperor passed over the usual steps and appointed him administration commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上諭曰：「浙江財賦地，自張鵬翮後，錢糧多蒙混，當秉公察核，不虧帑，不累民。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience, the emperor instructed: "Zhejiang is a land of fiscal revenue. Since Zhang Penghe, grain and funds have been much confused; you must examine impartially, neither shortchanging the treasury nor burdening the people.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience, the emperor told him: "Zhejiang is a province of revenue. Since Zhang Penghe's time, grain payments and tax accounts have been badly muddled. You must investigate fairly, neither letting the treasury suffer loss nor imposing hardship on the people.

sentences.zh: 布政使為一省表率，爾清廉，屬吏自皆守法。」

translations.literal: The administration commissioner is the model for a whole province; if you are incorruptible, subordinate officials will of themselves observe the law."
translations.idiomatic: As administration commissioner you set the standard for the whole province. If you remain incorrupt, your subordinates will follow the law of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 申喬頓首謝曰：「臣蒙皇上特擢，不黽勉為好官，請置重典。」

translations.literal: Shenqiao prostrated himself and replied: "Your subject has been specially promoted by Your Majesty; if I do not strive to be a good official, I ask to be subjected to severe punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty raised me far above my station. If I fail to prove myself a worthy official, let me be punished with the full severity of the law."

sentences.zh: 申喬上官，不挾幕客，治事皆躬親，例得火耗，悉屏不取。

translations.literal: When Shenqiao took up his post, he brought no private secretaries; in governing affairs he did everything personally; all meltage fees he was entitled to by regulation he rejected and did not take.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenqiao took office he brought no private secretaries and handled every matter himself. The meltage fees to which he was entitled by regulation he refused entirely.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上諭獎申喬居官清，能踐其言，就遷巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, the emperor issued instructions praising Shenqiao's integrity in office and his ability to fulfill his words, and he was promptly transferred to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year the emperor commended Shenqiao for his integrity in office and for keeping his word, and promoted him to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 布政使舊有貼解費，歲支不過十之五，申喬積二千餘金，封識以授代者，曰：「吾奏銷不名一錢，後將難繼，得此足辦一歲事，毋以擾民也。」

translations.literal: The administration commissioner formerly had forwarding fees, of which no more than half was disbursed yearly; Shenqiao accumulated more than two thousand taels, sealed and marked them, and handed them to his successor, saying: "In my accounts I have not claimed a single cash; successors will find that hard to match—having this is enough to cover one year's business, and you need not trouble the people."
translations.idiomatic: Administration commissioners once kept forwarding fees, of which only about half was spent each year. Shenqiao had saved more than two thousand taels, sealed them, and handed them to his successor, saying, "I never claimed a single cash in my accounts. Successors will find that hard to match. This sum is enough for one year's work—do not burden the people for it."

sentences.zh: 錢塘江潮齧塘，申喬令鎔鐵貫石，築子塘為護。

translations.literal: The Qiantang River tide was gnawing at the embankment; Shenqiao ordered iron melted and run through stones, and built subsidiary dikes for protection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiantang tide gnawed at the embankment, Shenqiao had iron cast through stone blocks and built subsidiary dikes as a buffer.

sentences.zh: 湖南鎮筸紅苗殺掠為民害，民走京師叩閽陳狀，給事中宋駿業因劾總督郭琇、巡撫金璽、提督林本植諱匿不為民去害，上命侍郎傅繼祖、甘國樞及申喬往按，盡發紅苗殺掠害民狀，琇等皆坐罷。

translations.literal: At Zhenbian in Hunan, Red Miao raiding and plundering harmed the people; the people went to the capital to beat the gate and present petitions. Censor Song Junye thereupon impeached Governor-General Guo Xiu, Governor Jin Xi, and Regional Commander Lin Benzhi for concealing the facts and failing to remove the harm to the people. The emperor ordered Vice Ministers Fu Jizu and Gan Guoshu, together with Shenqiao, to go investigate; they fully exposed the Red Miao raids harming the people, and Xiu and the others were all dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Red Miao bands at Zhenbian in Hunan were raiding and plundering, and the people fled to the capital to petition at the palace gates. Censor Song Junye impeached Governor-General Guo Xiu, Governor Jin Xi, and Regional Commander Lin Benzhi for covering up the crisis and failing to protect the people. The emperor sent Vice Ministers Fu Jizu and Gan Guoshu, together with Shenqiao, to investigate. They laid bare the full record of Miao raids, and Xiu and his colleagues were all removed from office.

sentences.zh: 調申喬偏沅巡撫。

translations.literal: Shenqiao was transferred to governor of Bianyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao was transferred to the governorship of Bianyuan.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，疏言與總督喻成龍檄衡永道張士可入苗洞宣撫，已聽命者二十餘寨，並與提督俞益謨發兵討諸不率命者。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, he memorialized that, together with Governor-General Yu Chenglong, he had ordered Zhang Shike of the Hengyong circuit to enter the Miao caves to pacify them; more than twenty stockades had already submitted, and together with Regional Commander Yu Yimo he had also sent troops to punish those who would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he reported that he and Governor-General Yu Chenglong had ordered Zhang Shike of the Hengyong circuit into the Miao hills to win submission. More than twenty stockades had already yielded, and he and Regional Commander Yu Yimo had also sent troops against those who refused.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書席爾達等率荊州駐防滿洲兵，並檄廣東、貴州、湖北三省提督，會成龍等進攻。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister Xi Erda and others to lead the Manchu garrison troops at Jingzhou, and also dispatched orders to the regional commanders of Guangdong, Guizhou, and Hubei to join Chenglong and the others in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minister Xi Erda and others to lead the Manchu garrison at Jingzhou, and instructed the regional commanders of Guangdong, Guizhou, and Hubei to join Chenglong in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 自龍椒洞至於天星寨，分道搜剿，斬悍苗千餘，三百餘寨咸聽命受約束，苗悉定。

translations.literal: From Longjiaodong to Tianxing Stockade they searched and suppressed by separate routes, beheading more than a thousand fierce Miao; more than three hundred stockades all submitted and accepted restraint, and the Miao were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: From Longjiaodong to Tianxing Stockade they swept the country by separate columns, killing more than a thousand hardened fighters. Over three hundred stockades submitted and accepted imperial restraint, and the Miao were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 申喬疏上善後諸事，移辰沅道駐其地。

translations.literal: Shenqiao memorialized on various matters of post-pacification administration and moved the Chenyuan circuit office to be stationed in that region.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao submitted a memorial on post-pacification measures and moved the Chenyuan circuit yamen to be stationed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 上獎徵苗諸將，貴州提督李芳述功最，並褒申喬強毅。

translations.literal: The emperor rewarded the generals who had campaigned against the Miao; Guizhou Regional Commander Li Fangshu had the greatest merit, and Shenqiao was also praised for his firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded the generals of the Miao campaign. Li Fangshu, regional commander of Guizhou, won the highest praise, and Shenqiao was commended for his firmness.

sentences.zh: 上南巡，申喬朝行在，上以潮南地偏遠，官吏私徵、加耗倍於他省，特詔申飭。

translations.literal: On the emperor's southern tour, Shenqiao attended at the traveling palace; because Hunan was a remote region where officials levied private exactions and surcharges ran to twice those of other provinces, a special edict was issued to admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's southern tour, Shenqiao presented himself at the traveling palace. Because Hunan was remote and officials there levied private exactions at surcharges twice the rate elsewhere, the emperor issued a special admonition.

sentences.zh: 申喬還，建上諭碑亭於通衢，示屬吏，並疏劾巴陵知縣李可昌等違例苛斂，奪官逮治。

translations.literal: When Shenqiao returned, he built a stele pavilion bearing the imperial instructions at a main thoroughfare to show subordinate officials, and also memorialized impeaching Baling magistrate Li Kechang and others for illegal exactions, stripping them of office and sending them for trial.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he erected a pavilion at a main crossroads bearing the imperial admonition for all subordinates to see, and memorialized against Baling magistrate Li Kechang and others for illegal levies, stripping them of office and ordering their arrest.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，申喬疏言：「清浪、平溪二衛地處山僻，請改米徵銀，俾省運費。」

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, Shenqiao memorialized: "The Qinglang and Pingxi two guards lie in remote mountains; I request that grain tax be collected in silver to save transport costs."
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year Shenqiao wrote, "The Qinglang and Pingxi guards lie in remote hill country. I ask that their grain levies be commuted to silver payment to save transport costs."

sentences.zh: 四十六年，疏言：「漕運旗丁舊有耗贈、行月銀米，於起運前預發。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, he memorialized: "Banner bondservants on the grain transport route formerly received meltage gifts and monthly silver and grain, issued in advance before transport began.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year he wrote, "Banner bondservants on the grain route once received meltage allowances and monthly silver and grain, paid out before transport began.

sentences.zh: 給事中戴嵩條奏俟至通州補發，意在防其虧缺。

translations.literal: Censor Dai Song submitted a clause memorial proposing that payment wait until Tongzhou for supplementary issue, intending to guard against shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dai Song proposed that these payments be held until Tongzhou and issued only as a supplement, intending to guard against shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 湖南運道遠於江、浙，例本無耗贈，惟恃行月銀米為轉運之資。

translations.literal: Hunan's transport route is farther than those of Jiangsu and Zhejiang; by regulation it had no meltage gifts in the first place and relied solely on monthly silver and grain as funds for transport.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's route is longer than those of Jiangsu and Zhejiang. By custom it received no meltage gifts at all and depended entirely on monthly silver and grain to move the grain.

sentences.zh: 今既扣存，窮丁不能涉遠，必致誤漕。

translations.literal: Now that these have been withheld, impoverished bondservants cannot travel the long distance, and the grain transport will certainly be disrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Now that these funds are withheld, the poorest bondservants cannot make the long haul, and the transport schedule will certainly slip.

sentences.zh: 請仍舊例預發。」

translations.literal: I request that the old rule of advance issue still be followed."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the old rule of advance payment be restored."

sentences.zh: 上許之，著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it and made it a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request and made it a standing order.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，命赴湖北按讞荊州同知王侃等侵蝕木稅，疏請裁港口渡私稅，荊州關稅部差如故。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, he was ordered to go to Hubei to investigate the case of Jingzhou vice prefect Wang Kan and others for embezzling timber tax; he memorialized requesting abolition of the private tax at Gangkou ferry, while the Jingzhou customs tax dispatched by the ministry would remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was sent to Hubei to try Jingzhou vice prefect Wang Kan and others for embezzling timber tax. He also asked that the private levy at Gangkou ferry be abolished, while Jingzhou customs taxes dispatched by the ministry would remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 申喬還，又請以靖州屬鸕鶿關稅併入辰州關。

translations.literal: When Shenqiao returned, he also requested that the Luzici Pass tax under Jingzhou be merged into the Chenzhou customs office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he also asked that the Luzici Pass tax under Jingzhou be folded into the Chenzhou customs office.

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「營兵給餉，每於正月支領，時地丁尚未開徵，挪移則累官，預徵則累民，請以隔歲餘存米石撥給兵餉。」

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: "When camp soldiers receive pay, it is issued every first month, when land tax has not yet been levied; shifting funds burdens officials, advance collection burdens the people—I request that surplus grain from the previous year be allocated for soldiers' pay."
translations.idiomatic: In a separate memorial he wrote, "Camp soldiers draw pay each first month, before the land tax is collected. Shifting funds burdens officials; advance collection burdens the people. I ask that surplus grain from the previous year be used for soldiers' pay."

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: The matter was also referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士宋大業祭告南嶽還京師，劾申喬輕褻御書，詔詰申喬。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Song Daye, returning to the capital after sacrificing at Mount Heng, impeached Shenqiao for slighting imperial writing; an edict was issued questioning Shenqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Song Daye, returning from sacrifices at Mount Heng, impeached Shenqiao for disrespect toward an imperial inscription. The emperor ordered Shenqiao to answer the charge.

sentences.zh: 申喬疏辨，並言：「大業初使湖南，餽金九千。

translations.literal: Shenqiao memorialized in defense, and also said: "On Daye's first mission to Hunan, he was presented nine thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao defended himself and added, "On Daye's first mission to Hunan he was offered nine thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 此次再使湖南，餽金五百，意不慊，札布政使董昭祚，言南嶽廟工餘銀毋報部。

translations.literal: On this second mission to Hunan, he was presented five hundred taels; dissatisfied, he sent a note to Administration Commissioner Dong Zhaozuo saying that surplus silver from the Mount Heng temple works should not be reported to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: On this second mission he was offered five hundred taels. Dissatisfied, he wrote Administration Commissioner Dong Zhaozuo that surplus silver from the Mount Heng temple works should not be reported to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 臣仍報部充餉，以是誣劾。」

translations.literal: Your subject still reported it to the ministry to supply military provisions; it is on this account that he falsely impeaches me."
translations.idiomatic: I still reported the sum to the ministry for military provisions. That is why he lodges this false charge."

sentences.zh: 大業坐奪官，申喬鐫五級留任。

translations.literal: Daye was stripped of office, and Shenqiao was demoted five ranks but retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Daye was stripped of office. Shenqiao was demoted five ranks but kept in his post.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，疏劾提督俞益謨取兵糧三十五石，詔詰益謨。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year, he memorialized impeaching Regional Commander Yu Yimo for taking thirty-five shi of soldiers' grain; an edict was issued questioning Yimo.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he impeached Regional Commander Yu Yimo for taking thirty-five shi of soldiers' grain. The emperor ordered Yimo to answer the charge.

sentences.zh: 益謨劾申喬苛刻，請並解官質訊。

translations.literal: Yimo impeached Shenqiao for harshness and requested that both be dismissed and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Yimo counter-impeached Shenqiao for harshness and asked that both men be dismissed and tried.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，上命尚書蕭永藻往按，永藻察申喬疏實，上為罷益謨，而命申喬還職。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, the emperor ordered Minister Xiao Yongzao to go investigate; Yongzao found Shenqiao's memorial substantiated, the emperor dismissed Yimo on that account, and ordered Shenqiao to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year the emperor sent Minister Xiao Yongzao to investigate. Yongzao found Shenqiao's charges substantiated. The emperor dismissed Yimo and ordered Shenqiao back to his post.

sentences.zh: 尋擢左都御史，諭曰：「申喬甚清廉，但有性氣，人皆畏其直。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief; the emperor instructed: "Shenqiao is very incorruptible, but he has a temper, and everyone fears his bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief. The emperor said, "Shenqiao is thoroughly incorrupt, but he has a temper, and everyone fears his bluntness.

sentences.zh: 朕察其無私，是以護惜之。」

translations.literal: I have observed that he is without private interest, and therefore protect and cherish him."
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that he has no private ends, and that is why I shield him."

sentences.zh: 五十年，疏請刻頒部行則例。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year, he memorialized requesting that ministry regulations in force be carved and promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he asked that the ministry's regulations in force be carved and promulgated.

sentences.zh: 劾編修戴名世所著南山集、孑遺錄有大逆語，下刑部，鞫實坐斬。

translations.literal: He impeached Compiler Dai Mingshi, author of Collected Writings from the Southern Mountains and Records of Survivors, for treasonous language; the case was sent to the Ministry of Punishments, and on investigation he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Compiler Dai Mingshi, whose Collected Writings from the Southern Mountains and Records of Survivors contained treasonous language. The case went to the Ministry of Punishments; inquiry proved the charge, and Dai was executed.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，疏請禁營兵冒名食糧；

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, he memorialized requesting prohibition of camp soldiers falsely claiming names to draw rations;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he asked that camp soldiers be barred from drawing rations under false names;

sentences.zh: 又言上普免各省地丁錢糧，惟潼關衛、大同府徵本色，不在​​蠲例，請如奉天、台灣例，一體蠲免：並允所請。

translations.literal: He also said that in the recent general exemption of land tax and corvée payments in every province, only Tongguan Guard and Datong Prefecture collected payments in kind and were not within the exemption; he requested that, following the precedents of Fengtian and Taiwan, they receive the same full exemption—and all his requests were approved.
translations.idiomatic: and noted that in the recent general land-tax exemption, only Tongguan Guard and Datong Prefecture still collected grain in kind and fell outside the relief. He asked that they be fully exempted like Fengtian and Taiwan. Both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 又疏言每歲農忙，京師當遵例停訟。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that every year during the busy farming season the capital should follow precedent and suspend lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that each year during the farming season the capital should suspend lawsuits as precedent allowed.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「農忙停訟，聽之似有理，實乃無益。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Suspending lawsuits during the farming season sounds reasonable, but in fact it is of no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Halting lawsuits during the farming season sounds reasonable, but it does no real good.

sentences.zh: 民非獨農也，商訟則廢生理，工訟則廢手藝。

translations.literal: The people are not only farmers: if merchants go to court, they abandon their livelihoods; if craftsmen go to court, they abandon their trades.
translations.idiomatic: The people are not all farmers. When merchants are drawn into litigation, their livelihoods suffer; when craftsmen are drawn into litigation, their trades suffer.

sentences.zh: 地方官不濫準詞狀，準則速結，訟亦少矣。

translations.literal: If local officials do not indiscriminately accept petitions, and when they do accept them conclude cases swiftly, lawsuits will also be fewer.
translations.idiomatic: If local officials refuse frivolous petitions and, when they do accept a case, bring it to a swift conclusion, lawsuits will naturally dwindle.

sentences.zh: 若但四月至七月停訟，而平日濫準詞狀，又復何益？

translations.literal: If you only suspend lawsuits from the fourth to the seventh month, yet on ordinary days indiscriminately accept petitions, what good would that do?
translations.idiomatic: If lawsuits are halted only from the fourth to the seventh month, while frivolous petitions are accepted as freely as ever the rest of the year, what would be gained?

sentences.zh: 且此四月至七月間，或有奸民詐害良善，冤向誰訴？

translations.literal: Moreover, between the fourth and seventh months, there may be scoundrels who defraud and harm honest people—to whom would the wronged appeal?
translations.idiomatic: And in those months from the fourth to the seventh, scoundrels may still defraud and harm honest people—where then would the wronged turn for redress?

sentences.zh: 八月以後，正當收​​穫，亦非閒時。

translations.literal: After the eighth month, it is just the time of harvest, which is also not idle season.
translations.idiomatic: After the eighth month comes the harvest, which is hardly an idle season either.

sentences.zh: 福建、廣東四季皆農時，豈終歲停訟乎？

translations.literal: In Fujian and Guangdong every season is farming season—are lawsuits to be suspended the whole year?
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian and Guangdong, every season is a farming season. Are lawsuits to be suspended all year long?

sentences.zh: 讀書當明理，事有益於民，朕即允行，否則斷乎不可也。」

translations.literal: In reading books one should understand principle; if a matter truly benefits the people, I will approve it, but otherwise it is absolutely impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship should teach one to see what is sound. If a measure truly benefits the people, I will approve it; otherwise it is out of the question."

sentences.zh: 五十二年，廣東飢，命往督平糶。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, Guangdong suffered famine, and he was ordered to go supervise the sale of grain at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year, when Guangdong was stricken by famine, he was ordered to go and supervise government grain sales at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 尋授戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，旗丁請指圈滄州民地，直隸巡撫趙弘燮議以旗退地另撥，部議不許。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, banner bondservants requested designation and enclosure of civilian land in Cangzhou; Zhili governor Zhao Hongxie proposed allocating withdrawn banner land instead, but the ministry deliberated and did not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year, banner bondservants petitioned to have civilian land in Cangzhou marked out and enclosed for their use. Zhili governor Zhao Hongxie proposed instead that land surrendered by the banners be allocated to them, but the ministry rejected the plan.

sentences.zh: 申喬言滄州民地有旨停圈，宜如弘燮議，上從之。

translations.literal: Shenqiao said that an imperial edict had already halted enclosure of Cangzhou civilian land, and that Hongxie's proposal should be followed; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao argued that an imperial edict had already suspended the enclosure of civilian land in Cangzhou, and that Hongxie's proposal ought to be adopted. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 時方鑄大錢，商人請納銀領易小錢送寶源局改鑄，命內務府會戶部議。

translations.literal: Large-value coin was then being cast, and merchants requested to pay in silver and receive small coins in exchange to send to the Baoyuan Bureau for recoining; the emperor ordered the Imperial Household Department to confer with the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the government was casting large-denomination coin, and merchants asked to pay in silver, receive small coin in exchange, and send it to the Baoyuan Bureau for recoining. The emperor ordered the Imperial Household Department to confer with the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 申喬言：「收小錢，有司責也，商人圖利，恐近藉端擾民，不可許。」

translations.literal: Shenqiao said: "Collecting small coin is the responsibility of officials; merchants seek profit, and I fear they will seize the opportunity nearby to harass the people—this cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao said, "Collecting small coin is the duty of the officials. Merchants are out for profit, and I fear they will use this as a pretext to harass the people. It must not be allowed."

sentences.zh: 而疏已上，議準申喬奏，請罷斥。

translations.literal: But the memorial had already been submitted; the deliberation approved Shenqiao's memorial, and he requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: By then his memorial had already gone up. The deliberation approved Shenqiao's recommendation, and he asked to be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 上召問狀，申喬言：「司官但送侍郎畫題，為所藐視，無顏复居職。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to inquire into the matter, and Shenqiao said: "The department officials only send memorials to the vice minister for signature, and I am held in contempt by them—I have no face to remain in office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to explain himself. Shenqiao said, "The department officials simply pass memorials to the vice minister for his signature. They hold me in contempt, and I am too ashamed to remain in office."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「君子懲忿窒慾，此語宜詳思。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "A gentleman restrains anger and checks desire—ponder these words carefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A gentleman restrains anger and checks desire. You should weigh those words carefully.

sentences.zh: 司官藐視，但當奏劾。

translations.literal: If department officials show contempt, you need only memorialize to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: If the department officials show contempt, you need only memorialize to impeach them.

sentences.zh: 爾性苛急，不能容人。

translations.literal: Your nature is harsh and impatient; you cannot tolerate others.
translations.idiomatic: Your temperament is harsh and impatient, and you cannot bear with others.

sentences.zh: 天地之大德曰生，非但不殺而已。

translations.literal: The greatest virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life—it is not merely refraining from killing.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life. It is not merely a matter of refraining from killing.

sentences.zh: 蓋於萬物皆養育而保全之。

translations.literal: It is rather to nurture and preserve all things.
translations.idiomatic: It is to nurture all things and keep them whole.

sentences.zh: 爾在官誠廉，然豈可恃廉而矯激乎？」

translations.literal: You are indeed incorruptible in office, but how can you rely on that integrity to indulge in harsh excess?"
translations.idiomatic: You are indeed incorruptible in office, but must you lean on that integrity to justify such harsh excess?"

sentences.zh: 命任事如故。

translations.literal: He was ordered to continue in his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to remain in office and carry on as before.

sentences.zh: 卒用申喬議，罷商人納銀領錢。

translations.literal: In the end Shenqiao's proposal was adopted, and the merchants' scheme to pay silver and receive coin was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Shenqiao's proposal prevailed, and the merchants' plan to pay silver and receive coin in exchange was abolished.

sentences.zh: 申喬子鳳詔，官太原知府。

translations.literal: Shenqiao's son Fengzhao served as prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao's son Fengzhao held the post of prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 上幸龍泉關，鳳詔入謁，上以申喬子優遇之。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Longquan Pass, Fengzhao came to audience; because he was Shenqiao's son, the emperor treated him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Longquan Pass, Fengzhao came to audience. Because he was Shenqiao's son, the emperor received him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 問巡撫噶禮賢否，鳳詔言噶禮清廉第一，上為擢噶禮江南總督。

translations.literal: He asked whether Governor Gali was worthy; Fengzhao said Gali was foremost in integrity, and on that account the emperor promoted Gali to governor-general of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether Governor Gali was a worthy man. Fengzhao replied that Gali was the most incorruptible of officials, and on that recommendation the emperor promoted Gali to governor-general of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 及噶禮以貪敗，上舉鳳詔問尚書張鵬翮，鵬翮言其貪。

translations.literal: When Gali later fell for corruption, the emperor cited Fengzhao and asked Minister Zhang Penghe about him; Penghe said he too was corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When Gali later fell in a corruption scandal, the emperor brought up Fengzhao and asked Minister Zhang Penghe about him. Penghe said that he too was corrupt.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，山西巡撫蘇克濟劾鳳詔受賕至三十餘萬，命奪官按治。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, Shanxi governor Sukeji impeached Fengzhao for accepting bribes of more than three hundred thousand, and the emperor ordered his dismissal and investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year, Shanxi governor Sukeji impeached Fengzhao for taking bribes totaling more than three hundred thousand taels. The emperor ordered him stripped of office and brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 申喬疏謝不能教子，請罷斥，上責其詞意忿激，非大臣體，命任事如故。

translations.literal: Shenqiao memorialized apologizing for failing to instruct his son and requesting dismissal; the emperor rebuked the vehemence of his language as unbecoming a senior minister and ordered him to remain in office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao submitted a memorial apologizing for his failure as a father and asking to be dismissed. The emperor rebuked the bitterness of his language as unworthy of a senior minister and ordered him to remain in office as before.

sentences.zh: 鳳詔坐贓罪至死。

translations.literal: Fengzhao was convicted of corruption and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhao was convicted of corruption and executed.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，以病乞休。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he requested retirement due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year, he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 上仍獎申喬清廉，令在官調治。

translations.literal: The emperor still praised Shenqiao's integrity and ordered him to rest and recover while remaining in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still commended Shenqiao for his integrity and ordered him to rest and recover while remaining in office.

sentences.zh: 鳳詔贓未清，命免追，並諭大學士，謂「速傳此旨，使其早知，庶服藥可效也」。

translations.literal: Fengzhao's unpaid restitution had not yet been settled; the emperor ordered that recovery not be pursued, and also instructed the grand secretaries, saying, "Transmit this edict quickly so that he may know soon, in the hope that taking medicine may then prove effective."
translations.idiomatic: Fengzhao's unpaid restitution had not yet been cleared, and the emperor ordered that it not be pursued. He also instructed the grand secretaries, saying, "Send this edict at once so that he may know of it soon; perhaps then his medicine will do some good."

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年七十有七，賜祭葬，諡恭毅。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he died, at the age of seventy-seven; he was granted funeral rites and the posthumous title Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of seventy-seven. He was granted state funeral honors and the posthumous title Gongyi, "Respectful and Resolute."

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，加贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年，湖廣總督邁柱疏劾屬吏虧帑，有申喬在偏沅時事，例當分償。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Huguang governor-general Mai Zhu memorialized impeaching a subordinate for treasury deficits, which included matters from Shenqiao's time as governor of Bianyuan; by regulation he was liable for shared restitution.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Huguang governor-general Mai Zhu memorialized impeaching a subordinate for treasury shortfalls that dated to Shenqiao's tenure as governor of Bianyuan. By regulation Shenqiao was liable to share in the restitution.

sentences.zh: 世宗特命免之。

translations.literal: The Yongzheng Emperor specially ordered that he be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor granted him a special exemption.

sentences.zh: 論曰：弘祚定賦役，文然修律例，皆為一代則，其績效鉅矣。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Hongzuo fixed tax and corvée, Wenran revised statutes and precedents—both established norms for their age, and their achievements were great.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Hongzuo fixed tax and corvée obligations, and Wenran revised statutes and precedents. Both set standards for their generation, and their achievements were immense.

sentences.zh: 象樞廉直謇謇，能規切用事大臣，尤言人所難言。

translations.literal: Xiangshu was upright, honest, and forthright; he could remonstrate with powerful ministers, and especially spoke what others found hard to say.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangshu was upright, honest, and unyielding. He could remonstrate with the powerful ministers of the day, and above all he spoke what others dared not say.

sentences.zh: 之弼意主於愛民，凡所獻替，皆切於民事。

translations.literal: Zhibi's purpose was above all to love the people; every proposal he offered or withdrew bore directly on the people's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibi's guiding purpose was love of the people. Every measure he proposed or withdrew was grounded in the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 申喬名輩差後，清介絕流輩，慷慨足以任國家之重。

translations.literal: Shenqiao was somewhat later in reputation, yet in integrity he surpassed his peers; with his generous spirit he was fully equal to the weight of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao belonged to a slightly later generation, yet in integrity he stood apart from his contemporaries. With his generous spirit he was fully equal to the burdens of state.

sentences.zh: 貞元之際，自據亂入昇平，開濟匡襄，諸臣與有力焉。

translations.literal: At the transition from disorder to peace, in moving from turmoil to prosperity, these ministers contributed forcefully to establishing order and assisting the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In that age when the realm was passing from disorder into peace, from turmoil into prosperity, these ministers played no small part in opening the way, restoring order, and supporting the throne.
